l-m-h2-b0d01-01.title: Log(a+b)=log a+log b dey always true?
l-m-h2-b0d01-01.goal: Check whether di claim log₂(a+b)=log₂a+log₂b dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e fail (a counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d01-01.material: Claim: for positive numbers a and b, log₂(a+b) = log₂a + log₂b always dey true. Find a and b wey show say dis claim dey wrong.
l-m-h2-b0d01-01.s.s1.prompt: Which a and b na counterexample to di claim?
l-m-h2-b0d01-01.s.s1.r.a: log₂4=2 and 1+1=2, so e dey true. E no be counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d01-01.s.s1.r.b: a+b=ab=9/2, so di two values equal. E no be counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d01-01.s.s1.r.c: a+b=ab=16/3, so di two values equal. E no be counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d01-01.s.s1.explain: If a=b=4, log₂8=3 but log₂4+log₂4=4. Sum of logarithms match product of di arguments.
l-m-h2-b0d01-01.s.s2.model.0: If a=b=4, log₂8=3 but log₂4+log₂4=4, so di two values different and e be counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d01-01.s.s2.model.1: log₂a+log₂b=log₂(ab), so dem equal only when a+b=ab. Because 4+4≠16, a=b=4 na counterexample.

l-m-h2-b0d01-10.title: Graphs of exponential function and logarithmic function dey always meet?
l-m-h2-b0d01-10.topic: Graphs of exponential and logarithmic functions
l-m-h2-b0d01-10.goal: Check whether the claim say graphs of y=aˣ and y=logₐx must meet always true, then find and explain one case where e fail (counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d01-10.material: Claim: if a>1, graphs of y=aˣ and y=logₐx must meet. Find a wey show say this claim wrong.
l-m-h2-b0d01-10.s.s1.prompt: Which a na counterexample to the claim?
l-m-h2-b0d01-10.s.s1.r.a: For x=1, aˣ>x, and for x=3, aˣ<x, so e meet y=x.
l-m-h2-b0d01-10.s.s1.r.b: For x=1, aˣ>x, and for x=2, aˣ<x, so e meet y=x.
l-m-h2-b0d01-10.s.s1.r.c: For x=2 and 4, aˣ=x, so the two graphs meet.
l-m-h2-b0d01-10.s.s1.explain: If a=2, then 2ˣ>x, so x>log₂x. 2ˣ dey above y=x and log₂x dey below am, so dem no meet.
l-m-h2-b0d01-10.s.s2.model.0: If a=2, then 2ˣ>x and x>log₂x, so y=2ˣ dey above y=x and y=log₂x dey below y=x, and dem no meet.
l-m-h2-b0d01-10.s.s2.model.1: 2ˣ dey always above y=x, and e inverse function log₂x dey always below y=x, so a=2, wey no get intersection, na the counterexample.

l-m-h2-b0d01-13.title: If θ big more, sinθ dey always big more too?
l-m-h2-b0d01-13.goal: Check whether the claim say sinθ also dey big as the angle big always true, then find and explain one case where e fail (counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d01-13.material: Claim: for 0°≤θ≤180°, anytime the angle θ big more, the value of sinθ must also big more. Find one change wey be counterexample to this claim.
l-m-h2-b0d01-13.s.s1.prompt: Which change go against the claim?
l-m-h2-b0d01-13.s.s1.r.a: sin10°<sin20°, so the value big more. E match the claim.
l-m-h2-b0d01-13.s.s1.r.b: E grow from 1/2 to √3/2. E match the claim.
l-m-h2-b0d01-13.s.s1.r.c: E grow from √2/2 to 1. E match the claim.
l-m-h2-b0d01-13.s.s1.explain: sin90°=1 and sin150°=1/2, so θ big more but the value small. After 90°, e dey reduce.
l-m-h2-b0d01-13.s.s2.model.0: θ grow from 90° to 150°, but sin90°=1 and sin150°=1/2 dey small, so e be counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d01-13.s.s2.model.1: sinθ dey grow until 90° and then e dey small, so the change from 90° to 150° na the counterexample wey break the claim.

l-m-h2-b0d01-21.title: If sin2A=sin2B, e mean say a=b?
l-m-h2-b0d01-21.goal: Check whether di claim say a=b if sin2A=sin2B dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e fail (a counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d01-21.material: Claim: for triangle ABC, if sin2A=sin2B, then a=b. Find two interior angles A and B wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-h2-b0d01-21.s.s1.prompt: Which A and B na counterexample to di claim?
l-m-h2-b0d01-21.s.s1.r.a: A=B, so a=b. Dis na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d01-21.s.s1.r.d: A=B, so a=b. Dis na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d01-21.s.s1.r.b: sin80°≠sin120°, so di condition no satisfy.
l-m-h2-b0d01-21.s.s1.explain: If A=20° and B=70°, then sin40°=sin140°, so di condition hold, but A≠B, so a≠b (A+B=90°).
l-m-h2-b0d01-21.s.s2.model.0: If A=20° and B=70°, then sin40°=sin140° satisfy di condition, but A≠B, so by di law of sines a≠b, wey make am a counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d01-21.s.s2.model.1: sin2A=sin2B also hold when 2A+2B=180°, so with 20° and 70°, where A+B=90°, one counterexample with a≠b show.

l-m-h2-b0d01-34.title: n²−n+11 Always Be Prime?
l-m-h2-b0d01-34.goal: Check whether di claim say n²−n+11 always be prime dey true every time, and find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d01-34.material: Claim: For every natural number n, n²−n+11 na prime. As we check from n=1, we get 11, 13, 17, 23, 31, all dem na prime.
l-m-h2-b0d01-34.s.s1.prompt: Which n na counterexample to di claim?
l-m-h2-b0d01-34.s.s1.r.a: 9−3+11=17 na prime, so e no be counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d01-34.s.s1.r.b: 25−5+11=31 na prime, so e no be counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d01-34.s.s1.r.c: 64−8+11=67 na prime, so e no be counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d01-34.s.s1.explain: When n=11, 11²−11+11=121=11×11, wey no be prime. Plenty cases still no be proof.
l-m-h2-b0d01-34.s.s2.model.0: When n=11, 11²−11+11=121=11×11, wey no be prime, so na counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d01-34.s.s2.model.1: Even though primes show for n=1 reach 10, n=11 give 121=11×11, so to get plenty cases no mean say e hold for every n.

l-m-h2-b0d02-06.goal: Check whether the claim say if x>y then log₂x²>log₂y² always true, then find and explain one case where e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d02-06.material: Claim: For real numbers x and y wey no be 0, if x>y then log₂x²>log₂y². Find x and y wey show say this claim wrong.
l-m-h2-b0d02-06.s.s1.r.b: Since 16>1, log₂16>log₂1. This one match the claim.
l-m-h2-b0d02-06.s.s1.r.c: Since 25>4, log₂25>log₂4. This one match the claim.
l-m-h2-b0d02-06.s.s1.r.d: Since 9>1, log₂9>log₂1. This one match the claim.
l-m-h2-b0d02-06.s.s1.explain: x=1>y=−3, but x²=1<9=y², so log₂1<log₂9. Squaring dey lose the information about the sign.
l-m-h2-b0d02-06.s.s2.model.0: x=1>y=−3, but x²=1 small pass y²=9, so log₂x²<log₂y², wey make am counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d02-06.s.s2.model.1: The log₂ function dey increase, but squaring dey make size of negative number big, so for x=1, y=−3, x²<y² and the claim break.

l-m-h2-b0d02-14.goal: Check whether di claim say angles wey get di same value of tanθ dey equal always dey true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d02-14.material: Claim: For 0≤θ<2π, two angles θ₁ and θ₂ wey get di same value of tanθ dey equal. Find two angles wey show say dis claim wrong.

l-m-h2-b0d02-14.s.s1.r.d: Di tan values na 1 and −1, dem different, so e no meet di condition.
l-m-h2-b0d02-14.s.s1.explain: tan(π/4)=1 and tan(5π/4)=1, but di two angles different. Di period of tan na π.
l-m-h2-b0d02-14.s.s2.model.0: tan(π/4)=1 and tan(5π/4)=1 get di same value but di two angles different, so na counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d02-14.s.s2.model.1: Di period of tanθ na π, so if you add π to θ, di value no change, and different angles dey wey get di same value, like π/4 and 5π/4.

l-m-h2-b0d04-21.title: Di definite integral of increasing function dey always positive?
l-m-h2-b0d04-21.goal: Check whether di claim "di definite integral of increasing function dey always positive" dey always true, and find one case wey e fail (a counterexample) and explain am.
l-m-h2-b0d04-21.material: Claim: If f na increasing function, di definite integral of f dey positive for any interval wey a<b. Find one case wey show say dis claim no correct.
l-m-h2-b0d04-21.s.s1.r.a: Di definite integral na 2, wey dey positive. E be example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d04-21.s.s1.r.c: Di definite integral na 2, wey dey positive. E be example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d04-21.s.s1.r.d: Di definite integral na 4, wey dey positive. E be example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d04-21.s.s1.explain: If you integrate f(x)=x over [−2,1] e give (1−4)/2=−3/2. Even if function dey increase, di integral fit negative when di part wey dey under di x-axis big pass.
l-m-h2-b0d04-21.s.s2.model.0: f(x)=x dey increase, but im definite integral over [−2,1] na (1²−(−2)²)/2=−3/2, wey negative, so e be counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d04-21.s.s2.model.1: Because di graph for x<0 dey under di x-axis and dat area big pass, di definite integral become negative and di claim break.

l-m-h2-b0d05-01.title: Di permutation count dey always bigger pass di combination count?
l-m-h2-b0d05-01.goal: Check whether di claim "nPr dey always bigger pass nCr" dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e no work (a counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d05-01.material: Claim: Wen you dey choose r from n different things, di number of permutations nPr dey always bigger pass di number of combinations nCr. Find one case wey show say dis claim no correct.
l-m-h2-b0d05-01.s.s1.r.b: 24 wit 4, so di permutation count bigger. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d05-01.s.s1.r.c: 42 wit 21, so di permutation count bigger. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d05-01.s.s1.r.d: 5P2=20 and 5C2=10, so di permutation count bigger. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d05-01.s.s1.explain: 6P1=6 and 6C1=6, so dem equal. Wen r=1, nPr=nCr=n, so di permutation count no bigger.
l-m-h2-b0d05-01.s.s2.model.0: 6P1=6 and 6C1=6, so di two values equal and di claim say di permutation count bigger don break, so na counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d05-01.s.s2.model.1: Wen r=1, dem dey choose only one, so order no get meaning and nPr and nCr go equal. Na why 6P1 and 6C1 be di counterexample.

l-m-h2-b0d05-02.title: Wen di addition rule dey break?
l-m-h2-b0d05-02.goal: Check whether di claim "just add di two numbers of cases" dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e no work (a counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d05-02.material: Claim: If event A fit happen in m ways and event B fit happen in n ways, then 'A or B' fit happen in m+n ways, always. Check am with di numbers 1 to 12.
l-m-h2-b0d05-02.s.s1.r.a: 6 odd numbers dey and 3 multiples of 4 dey with no overlap, so na 9, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d05-02.s.s1.r.b: Dem be 5, 10 and 7, so 2+1=3 with no overlap, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d05-02.s.s1.r.c: 5 primes dey and 6 composites dey with no overlap, so na 11, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d05-02.s.s1.explain: If you add 4 multiples of 3 and 3 multiples of 4 e give 7, but dem count 12 two times, so di real number na 6 ways.
l-m-h2-b0d05-02.s.s2.model.0: 12 na multiple of 3 and multiple of 4 at di same time, so dem count am two times, and di real number na 6 ways, no be 4+3=7. So na counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d05-02.s.s2.model.1: Because of di overlapping number 12, if you just add, e give 7 ways, wey no be di real 6 ways. Dis case na counterexample to di claim.

l-m-h2-b0d05-03.title: P(A|B) and P(B|A) dey always equal?
l-m-h2-b0d05-03.topic: Conditional probability (chance wey depend on something)
l-m-h2-b0d05-03.goal: Check whether di claim "P(A|B) and P(B|A) dey always equal" dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e no work (a counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d05-03.material: Claim: For two events A and B, di conditional probabilities P(A|B) and P(B|A) dey always equal. Test dis claim with di pairs of events below for one roll of a die.
l-m-h2-b0d05-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose di events A and B wey go against di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d05-03.s.s1.r.b: Both get 3 outcomes and A∩B={1, 3}, so both values equal for 2/3.
l-m-h2-b0d05-03.s.s1.o.c: A: 3 or less, B: 4 or more
l-m-h2-b0d05-03.s.s1.r.c: A∩B na empty set, so both values equal for 0.
l-m-h2-b0d05-03.s.s1.r.d: Dem be di same event, so both values equal for 1.
l-m-h2-b0d05-03.s.s1.explain: P(A|B)=n(A∩B)/n(B) and P(B|A)=n(A∩B)/n(A). For even and 4 or less, dem different: 1/2 and 2/3.
l-m-h2-b0d05-03.s.s2.model.0: If A=even and B=4 or less, then P(A|B)=2/4=1/2 and P(B|A)=2/3, so di two values different. So na counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d05-03.s.s2.model.1: Di denominators different, n(B)=4 and n(A)=3, so even if A∩B na di same 2 outcomes, di two conditional probabilities still different.

l-m-h2-b0d05-04.title: If events dey mutually exclusive, dem independent?
l-m-h2-b0d05-04.goal: Check whether di claim "if events dey mutually exclusive, dem independent" dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e no work (a counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d05-04.material: Claim: Two mutually exclusive events A and B dey always independent. Independence mean say P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B) hold. Think about di case wey di probabilities of two mutually exclusive events be as dem dey below.
l-m-h2-b0d05-04.s.s1.r.a: P(A∩B)=0 and P(A)P(B)=0, so dem equal and di events independent.
l-m-h2-b0d05-04.s.s1.r.b: P(A∩B)=0 and P(A)P(B)=0, so dem equal and di events independent.
l-m-h2-b0d05-04.s.s1.r.d: Both values equal for 0, so dem independent.
l-m-h2-b0d05-04.s.s1.explain: If dem mutually exclusive, P(A∩B)=0. But P(A)P(B)=0.12, so dem no equal and di events no independent.
l-m-h2-b0d05-04.s.s2.model.0: Since dem mutually exclusive, P(A∩B)=0, but P(A)P(B)=0.3×0.4=0.12 different, so dem no independent and na counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d05-04.s.s2.model.1: If both probabilities pass 0, di product too no be 0, so e no fit equal P(A∩B)=0. So dem no independent.

l-m-h2-b0d05-05.title: Binomial distributions wey get di same mean: di variance too dey same?
l-m-h2-b0d05-05.goal: Check whether di claim "if di means equal, di variances equal" dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e no work (a counterexample).
l-m-h2-b0d05-05.material: Claim: Two binomial distributions wey get di same mean too get di same variance. Di mean of binomial distribution B(n, p) na np and di variance na np(1-p). Test dis claim with di pairs below.
l-m-h2-b0d05-05.s.s1.r.a: Di means different, 5 and 3, so e no fit test di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d05-05.s.s1.r.c: Di means different, 10 and 4, so e no fit test di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d05-05.s.s1.r.d: Di means different, 3 and 6, so e no fit test di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d05-05.s.s1.explain: Both get mean 5, but di variances different: 10×0.5×0.5=2.5 and 20×0.25×0.75=3.75.
l-m-h2-b0d05-05.s.s2.model.0: Di means of di two distributions na 5 both, but di variances na 2.5 and 3.75, so di claim break and na counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d05-05.s.s2.model.1: Even if di mean np dey di same, if p change, np(1-p) go change, so B(10, 0.5) and B(20, 0.25) get different variances.

l-m-h2-b0d06-01.title: N! ways dey always to arrange letters?
l-m-h2-b0d06-01.goal: Check whether di claim 'di number of ways to arrange n letters na n!' dey always true, then find one case wey e no true (a counterexample) and explain am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-01.material: Claim: di number of ways to arrange n letters for one row na always n!. Test dis claim with arrangements wey use all di letters of di words below.
l-m-h2-b0d06-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose di word wey contradict di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-01.s.s1.r.a: Dis na 5 different letters, so 5!=120 ways, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-01.s.s1.r.c: Dis na 4 different letters, so 4!=24 ways, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-01.s.s1.r.d: Dis na 4 different letters, so 4!=24 ways, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-01.s.s1.explain: LEVEL get two L's and two E's, so arrangements wey look di same dey show. E na 5!/(2!2!)=30 ways, no be 5!=120.
l-m-h2-b0d06-01.s.s2.model.0: LEVEL get 2 L's and 2 E's, so if you swap dem e give di same arrangement, so e na 30 ways, no be 120. Dat one make am counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d06-01.s.s2.model.1: If identical letters dey, to count with 5! count some two times, so e become 5!/(2!2!)=30, wey differ from n!.

l-m-h2-b0d06-02.goal: Check whether di claim 'di expected value na value wey X fit take' dey always true, then find one case wey e no true (a counterexample) and explain am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-02.material: Claim: di expected value of random variable X na always one of di values wey X fit really take. Test di claim by finding di expected values of di random variables below.
l-m-h2-b0d06-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose di random variable wey contradict di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-02.s.s1.o.a: Number of heads when dem toss 2 coins
l-m-h2-b0d06-02.s.s1.r.a: Di values na 0, 1, 2, and di expected value 1 na possible value.
l-m-h2-b0d06-02.s.s1.o.b: Number of heads when dem toss 6 coins
l-m-h2-b0d06-02.s.s1.r.b: Di values na 0~6, and di expected value 3 na possible value.
l-m-h2-b0d06-02.s.s1.o.c: Number of heads when dem toss 4 coins
l-m-h2-b0d06-02.s.s1.r.c: Di values na 0~4, and di expected value 2 na possible value.
l-m-h2-b0d06-02.s.s1.explain: Di expected value of die na (1+2+3+4+5+6)/6=3.5. Die dey show integer, so 3.5 no fit show.
l-m-h2-b0d06-02.s.s2.model.0: Di expected value of die na 3.5, but die dey show only di integers 1 to 6, so 3.5 no fit show. Dat one make am counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d06-02.s.s2.model.1: Di expected value na weighted average of di values, so e fit dey between possible values. 3.5 dey between 3 and 4, so di claim break.

l-m-h2-b0d06-03.title: Big standard deviation dey always make probability small?
l-m-h2-b0d06-03.goal: Check whether di claim 'if σ big, di interval probability small' dey always true, then find one case wey e no true (a counterexample) and explain am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-03.material: Claim: for two normal distributions wey get di same mean, di one wey get bigger standard deviation get smaller probability for any interval. Compare di distribution wey get mean 0 and standard deviation 1 with di one wey get standard deviation 2.
l-m-h2-b0d06-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose di interval wey contradict di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-03.s.s1.r.a: Around 0.38 when σ=1 and around 0.20 when σ=2, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-03.s.s1.r.c: Around 0.68 when σ=1 and around 0.38 when σ=2, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-03.s.s1.r.d: Around 0.95 when σ=1 and around 0.68 when σ=2, wey fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-03.s.s1.explain: X≥3 na tail. E na around 0.001 when σ=1 and around 0.067 when σ=2, so di bigger σ give di bigger value.
l-m-h2-b0d06-03.s.s2.model.0: X≥3 na tail interval, so e na around 0.067 when σ=2, bigger pass around 0.001 when σ=1. Di claim break, so e be counterexample.
l-m-h2-b0d06-03.s.s2.model.1: When σ big, di curve spread out wide, so di probability for di central interval dey small but di tail probability dey big. Na why X≥3 be counterexample.

l-m-h2-b0d06-04.title: Di coefficient for expansion dey always be nCr?
l-m-h2-b0d06-04.goal: Check whether di claim "di coefficient of xʳ na always nCr" dey always true, then find one case wey e no true (a counterexample) and explain am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-04.material: Claim: when dem expand (ax+b)ⁿ, di coefficient of xʳ na always di binomial coefficient nCr. Test di claim by comparing di coefficient of di given term for each expansion below with nCr.
l-m-h2-b0d06-04.s.s1.prompt: Choose di expansion wey go against di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-04.s.s1.r.b: Di coefficient na 4C2=6, so e fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-04.s.s1.r.c: Di coefficient na 6C3=20, so e fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-04.s.s1.r.d: Di coefficient na 5C4=5, so e fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-04.s.s1.explain: Di coefficient of di x² term of (2x+1)³ na 3C2×2²=12. E differ from 3C2=3 because di coefficient 2 of x dey multiply inside as square.
l-m-h2-b0d06-04.s.s2.model.0: Di x² term of (2x+1)³ na 3C2×2²=12, but 3C2=3, so di coefficients differ. Na why dis expansion be counterexample to di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-04.s.s2.model.1: Because di coefficient 2 of x dey multiply in r times (raised to di power r), di coefficient become bigger pass nCr. So di x² term of (2x+1)³ na 12, wey differ from 3C2.

l-m-h2-b0d06-05.title: Di sample mean dey always equal di population mean?
l-m-h2-b0d06-05.goal: Check whether di claim "di sample mean equal di population mean" dey always true, then find one case wey e no true (a counterexample) and explain am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-05.material: Claim: di mean of sample wey dem draw from population dey always equal di population mean. Di population na {2, 4, 6}, so di population mean na 4. Test di claim with samples wey dem draw from dis population.
l-m-h2-b0d06-05.s.s1.prompt: Choose di sample wey go against di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-05.s.s1.r.a: Di sample mean na 4, equal to di population mean, so e fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-05.s.s1.r.b: Di sample mean na 4, equal to di population mean, so e fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-05.s.s1.r.d: Di sample mean na 4, equal to di population mean, so e fit di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-05.s.s1.explain: Di mean of {2, 4} na 3, wey different from di population mean 4. Di sample mean fit different from one sample to another.
l-m-h2-b0d06-05.s.s2.model.0: Di mean of sample {2, 4} na 3, but di population mean na 4, so di two values different. Na why dis sample be counterexample to di claim.
l-m-h2-b0d06-05.s.s2.model.1: Di mean dey change depending on which values dem draw enter di sample, so sample mean wey different from di population mean 4, like {2, 4}, fit happen.

l-m-h2-b0d01-04.title: Find di criterion wey decide how many n-th roots dey
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.goal: To find out di number of real numbers x wey satisfy xⁿ=a, decide which criterion (information) dem really need, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.material: For real number a and integer n wey be at least 2, we wan know how many real numbers x satisfy xⁿ=a. Which information dem really need?
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.s.s1.prompt: Which information dem really need to know di number of real numbers x?
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.s.s1.o.a: Whether a na integer or not
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.s.s1.r.a: Even if a no be integer, di sign and whether n na even or odd decide di number.
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.s.s1.r.b: Di last digit no decide di number of real numbers x.
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.s.s1.o.c: Whether n na even or odd, and di sign of a
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.s.s1.o.d: Whether n big pass 10 or small pass 10
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.s.s1.r.d: Wetin matter na whether n na even or odd, no be how big n be.
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.s.s1.explain: If n na odd, one dey. If n na even, two dey when a>0, one dey when a=0, and none dey when a<0.
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.s.s2.model.0: If n na even, 2 dey when a>0 and 0 dey when a<0, and if n na odd, 1 always dey. So di parity of n and di sign of a na wetin dem really need.
l-m-h2-b0d01-04.s.s2.model.1: x²=4 get 2, but x²=−4 no get any, and x³=−8 get 1. Di number dey change with parity and sign, so dis two pieces of information na di criterion.

l-m-h2-b0d01-14.title: Information wey truly needed to decide the sign of sinθ
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.goal: To know the signs of sinθ and cosθ, decide which criterion (information) truly needed, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.material: For general angle θ, we wan know whether sinθ and cosθ positive or negative. Which information truly needed?
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.s.s1.prompt: Which information truly needed to know the sign?
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.s.s1.o.a: How many turns the terminal side don make
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.s.s1.r.a: The number of turns no get anything to do with the sign. The position of the terminal side na wetin matter.
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.s.s1.o.b: The distance of one point for the terminal side from the origin
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.s.s1.r.b: That distance r always positive, so e no fit change the sign.
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.s.s1.o.c: Whether θ na whole number of degrees (°)
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.s.s1.r.c: Whether e na whole number or no be so, the position of the terminal side dey decide the sign.
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.s.s1.o.d: The quadrant where the terminal side dey
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.s.s1.explain: For sinθ=y/r and cosθ=x/r, r>0, so the signs dey decided by the signs of x and y of the point, wey be the quadrant.
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.s.s2.model.0: sinθ=y/r and cosθ=x/r, and r always positive, so the signs dey decided by the signs of x and y of the point for the terminal side, wey be the quadrant.
l-m-h2-b0d01-14.s.s2.model.1: Even if the distance or the number of turns different, the sign na the same for the same quadrant, so which quadrant the terminal side dey na the information wey truly needed.

l-m-h2-b0d01-22.title: Di criterion wey separate di law of sines from di law of cosines
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.topic: Law of sines and law of cosines
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.goal: To know which law to use first when you dey solve a triangle, decide which criterion (information) you really need, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.material: When dem give three parts of a triangle (sides and angles), we wan find di rest. Find di criterion wey go decide whether di first law to use na di law of sines or di law of cosines.
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.s.s1.o.a: Whether di triangle near right angle
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.s.s1.r.a: Dem dey choose di law by di same criterion whether right angle dey or no dey.
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.s.s1.o.b: Whether di angle size dey for degrees
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.s.s1.r.b: Di law na di same whether na degrees or radians.
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.s.s1.o.c: Whether di given values na integers
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.s.s1.r.c: To be integer or not no be di criterion to choose di law.
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.s.s1.o.d: Whether dem give a side and its opposite angle as a pair
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.s.s1.explain: If one pair of a side and its opposite angle dey, use di law of sines, and if two sides and di included angle dey or three sides dey, use di law of cosines.
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.s.s2.model.0: If dem give a side and its opposite angle as a pair, you fit use di ratio of di law of sines, and if no such pair dey, you must use di law of cosines, so dis pair na di criterion.
l-m-h2-b0d01-22.s.s2.model.1: When no corresponding pair dey, like two sides and di included angle or three sides, you no fit make di ratio of di law of sines, so dem dey use di law of cosines first.

l-m-h2-b0d01-25.title: Di criterion wey decide whether a geometric sequence dey increase
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.goal: To know whether a geometric sequence na increasing sequence, decide which criterion (information) you really need, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.material: We wan know whether di geometric sequence aₙ=a·rⁿ⁻¹ (a≠0, r>0) na increasing sequence. Which information we really need?
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.s.s1.prompt: Which information we really need to know whether e dey increase?
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.s.s1.o.a: Only whether di common ratio big pass 1
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.s.s1.r.a: If di first term na negative, e go dey reduce even if di common ratio big pass 1.
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.s.s1.o.b: Whether di first term na integer
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.s.s1.r.b: Whether e be integer no get anything to do with increasing or decreasing.
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.s.s1.o.c: Di sum of di first three terms
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.s.s1.r.c: Di sum alone no dey tell you whether di terms dey get bigger.
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.s.s1.o.d: Di sign of di first term and whether di common ratio big pass 1
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.s.s1.explain: If a>0, e dey increase when r>1, and if a<0, e dey increase when 0<r<1. You need both di sign and di size of r.
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.s.s2.model.0: If a>0 and r>1, e dey increase, and if a<0, e dey increase when 0<r<1, so we really need di sign of di first term and whether di common ratio big pass 1.
l-m-h2-b0d01-25.s.s2.model.1: −3, −6, −12 get common ratio of 2 but e dey reduce, so di common ratio alone no reach. You also need to know di sign of di first term.

l-m-h2-b0d02-01.title: Wetin condition dey needed make a logarithm get meaning?
l-m-h2-b0d02-01.goal: Decide which criteria (information) dem must get to find di condition make log_a b get meaning, and explain why you choose dem.
l-m-h2-b0d02-01.material: For di logarithm log_a b, a na di base and b na di argument. We wan decide which conditions dem need together make this logarithm turn one real value.
l-m-h2-b0d02-01.s.s1.prompt: Which choice group di needed conditions correct?
l-m-h2-b0d02-01.s.s1.r.a: If di base negative, aˣ no fit get meaning for every real number x.
l-m-h2-b0d02-01.s.s1.r.c: If a=1, every power of 1 na always 1, so log₁5 no get value.
l-m-h2-b0d02-01.s.s1.r.d: Cases like log_(1/2)4=−2, wey a<1 or b<1, get meaning too.
l-m-h2-b0d02-01.s.s1.explain: Di base must be positive and no be 1, and di argument must be positive.
l-m-h2-b0d02-01.s.s2.model.0: If di base na 1, 1ˣ na always 1, and if e negative, aˣ no get meaning, so dem need a>0 and a≠1. Since aˣ>0, dem need b>0 too.
l-m-h2-b0d02-01.s.s2.model.1: Since aˣ always positive, di argument must satisfy b>0, and if di base na 1, any x give 1, so a≠1 dey required.

l-m-h2-b0d02-15.title: Di Value Wey Decide Di Period of y=a sin(bx+c)+d
l-m-h2-b0d02-15.goal: Decide which criteria (information) you must get to find di coefficient wey decide di period, and explain why you choose dem.
l-m-h2-b0d02-15.material: We wan find di period from a graph wey be like y=a sin(bx+c)+d. Which one among a, b, c, d you must get? (a and b no be 0.)
l-m-h2-b0d02-15.s.s1.prompt: Which value you must know to know di period?
l-m-h2-b0d02-15.s.s1.r.a: a dey decide di amplitude. E no get anything to do with di period.
l-m-h2-b0d02-15.s.s1.r.b: c only dey decide di left-right shift. Di period still dey di same.
l-m-h2-b0d02-15.s.s1.r.c: d only dey decide di up-down shift. Di period still dey di same.
l-m-h2-b0d02-15.s.s1.explain: Di period na 2π/|b|. a dey decide di amplitude, c di left-right shift, and d di up-down shift.
l-m-h2-b0d02-15.s.s2.model.0: Di period na 2π/|b| decide am, so you only need to know di absolute value of b. a, c, and d only dey move or make di shape big.
l-m-h2-b0d02-15.s.s2.model.1: To stretch di graph or move am up and down no dey change di horizontal length of one repeat, so na only b, wey dey squeeze di horizontal direction, dey decide di period.

l-m-h2-b0d02-25.title: Criteria to choose a sum formula for a sequence
l-m-h2-b0d02-25.goal: Work out which criterion (information) you really need to choose a sum formula, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d02-25.material: We wan find di sum of di first plenty terms of di sequence 2, 4, 8, 16, … Find di criterion wey go decide whether to use di arithmetic sequence sum formula or di geometric sequence sum formula.
l-m-h2-b0d02-25.s.s1.prompt: Which information we really need to choose di formula?

l-m-h2-b0d02-25.s.s1.o.b: Whether di first term na natural number
l-m-h2-b0d02-25.s.s1.r.b: Whether e be natural number no be criterion to choose formula.
l-m-h2-b0d02-25.s.s1.o.c: Whether all di terms dey positive
l-m-h2-b0d02-25.s.s1.r.c: Dem dey use di same formula even when di signs differ. You need to look di difference or di ratio.

l-m-h2-b0d02-25.s.s1.explain: If di difference of neighboring terms dey constant, e be arithmetic; if di ratio dey constant, e be geometric. For 2, 4, 8, 16, di ratio dey constant at 2.
l-m-h2-b0d02-25.s.s2.model.0: If di difference of neighboring terms dey constant, use di arithmetic sequence formula; if di ratio dey constant, use di geometric sequence formula, so di difference or ratio na di criterion.
l-m-h2-b0d02-25.s.s2.model.1: For 2, 4, 8, 16 di differences dey change as 2, 4, 8, but di ratio na always 2, so you suppose choose di geometric sequence sum formula.

l-m-h2-b0d02-36.goal: Work out which criterion (information) dem really need to prove statement wey hold for n≥3 by induction, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d02-36.material: We wan prove di statement "2ⁿ>2n+1 for natural numbers n≥3" by mathematical induction. Make we work out which checks dem really need.
l-m-h2-b0d02-36.s.s1.prompt: Which checks dem really need for di proof?
l-m-h2-b0d02-36.s.s1.o.a: E hold for n=3, and from k go k+1 (k≥3)
l-m-h2-b0d02-36.s.s1.o.b: Show say e false for n=1 and 2
l-m-h2-b0d02-36.s.s1.r.b: To show say e false for n wey outside di range no needed for di proof.
l-m-h2-b0d02-36.s.s1.o.c: Calculate one by one reach n=100
l-m-h2-b0d02-36.s.s1.r.c: Limited amount of calculation no fit show am for every n.

l-m-h2-b0d02-36.s.s1.r.d: For n=1, 2>3 false. Di starting point na n=3.
l-m-h2-b0d02-36.s.s1.explain: Di starting point na n=3. Check 8>7 for n=3, and show say for k≥3, if e hold for k, e hold for k+1 too.
l-m-h2-b0d02-36.s.s2.model.0: Di range of di statement na n≥3, so di base step na to check 8>7 for n=3, and dem need induction step wey show k→k+1 for k≥3.
l-m-h2-b0d02-36.s.s2.model.1: Di statement false for n=1 and 2, so you must set di starting point for n=3, and then one step must dey wey go from k to k+1.

l-m-h2-b0d03-02.title: Wetin decide di limit of fraction expression as x dey big?
l-m-h2-b0d03-02.goal: Work out which criterion (information) dem really need to find di limit of rational expression as x→∞, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d03-02.material: Think about expression like (3x²+5x−2)/(2x²−7), where di numerator and denominator na polynomials. Which information we suppose look to find di limit as x dey grow without end?
l-m-h2-b0d03-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose di information wey dem really need to decide di limit.
l-m-h2-b0d03-02.s.s1.o.a: Di sum of di coefficients of all di terms
l-m-h2-b0d03-02.s.s1.r.a: Di coefficients of lower-degree terms no decide di limit.
l-m-h2-b0d03-02.s.s1.o.b: Di degrees and coefficients of di highest-degree terms of di numerator and denominator

l-m-h2-b0d03-02.s.s1.r.c: Na x→∞ problem be this, so di value for x=0 no matter.

l-m-h2-b0d03-02.s.s1.r.d: Di effect of constant terms dey small more as x dey big.
l-m-h2-b0d03-02.s.s1.explain: When x big well well, di highest-degree term dey control di expression. If di degrees equal, e go near di ratio of di coefficients, 3/2.
l-m-h2-b0d03-02.s.s2.model.0: Di highest-degree terms dey control di expression, like di numerator 3x² and di denominator 2x², so di ratio of these coefficients, 3/2, na di limit.
l-m-h2-b0d03-02.s.s2.model.1: When x big well well, you fit ignore lower-degree terms, so if you know only di degrees and coefficients of di highest-degree terms, you don decide di limit.

l-m-h2-b0d03-09.title: Which information dem need for di limit of |x|/x for x=0?
l-m-h2-b0d03-09.goal: Work out which criterion (information) dem really need to know whether |x|/x get limit for x=0, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d03-09.material: We get f(x)=|x|/x (x≠0). We wan find out whether f(x) get limit as x dey near 0.
l-m-h2-b0d03-09.s.s1.o.a: Di values as x dey near 0 from di right and from di left
l-m-h2-b0d03-09.s.s1.r.b: Limit no get anything to do with di value for x=0 itself.
l-m-h2-b0d03-09.s.s1.r.c: The maximum value alone no dey tell you the value wey e dey approach near x=0.
l-m-h2-b0d03-09.s.s1.o.d: The value of f(x) for x=1
l-m-h2-b0d03-09.s.s1.r.d: The value for one far-off point no get anything to do with the limit.
l-m-h2-b0d03-09.s.s1.explain: E be 1 if x>0 and −1 if x<0. The right-hand limit 1 and the left-hand limit −1 different, so the limit no exist.
l-m-h2-b0d03-09.s.s2.model.0: Limit dey exist only if the values wey e dey approach from both sides as x dey get close to 0 na the same, so you must look the left and right values separately.
l-m-h2-b0d03-09.s.s2.model.1: f(0) no define and e no get anything to do with the limit, so you must compare the values from both sides, like 1 for the right and −1 for the left.

l-m-h2-b0d03-13.title: Wetin truly needed for the equation of tangent line?
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.goal: Work out which criterion (information) truly needed to find the equation of the tangent line for one point on curve, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.material: We wan write the equation of the tangent line for one point on the curve y=f(x). Think about which information truly needed.
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.s.s1.o.a: The point where the curve meet the x-axis
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.s.s1.r.a: The intersection with the x-axis no get direct relation to the tangent line.
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.s.s1.o.b: The x-coordinate of the point of tangency and the derivative for that point
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.s.s1.o.c: Only the function value for x=0
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.s.s1.r.c: You need the value and the slope for the point of tangency.
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.s.s1.o.d: The maximum value of the function
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.s.s1.r.d: Dem no need the maximum value to determine the tangent line.
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.s.s1.explain: Point of tangency (the x-coordinate and function value) and the slope f'(a) dey determine tangent line. Write am as y−f(a)=f'(a)(x−a).
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.s.s2.model.0: One point wey line pass through and e slope dey determine the line, and the coordinates of the point of tangency and the derivative for that point na exactly those two, na why dem needed.
l-m-h2-b0d03-13.s.s2.model.1: The slope na the derivative for the point of tangency, so you must know the x-coordinate of the point of tangency and find f'(a) to write the tangent line equation.

l-m-h2-b0d03-23.s.s1.prompt: Choose di information wey you need to know first.
l-m-h2-b0d03-23.s.s1.r.a: Di value for one point alone no tell you di sign for di whole interval.
l-m-h2-b0d03-23.s.s1.o.b: Whether di minimum value of f na integer

l-m-h2-b0d03-23.s.s1.explain: If di graph dey below di x-axis, di definite integral go negative, so you gats change di sign to get di area. For here, −(−36)=36.
l-m-h2-b0d03-23.s.s2.model.0: Di definite integral dey count di part below di x-axis as negative, so you need to know di sign of f for di interval to turn am to area.
l-m-h2-b0d03-23.s.s2.model.1: f na 0 for 0 and 6 and negative for between, so you must put − sign for di value of di definite integral to get di area. Na why you check di sign first.

l-m-h2-b0d04-12.material: Wetin we know na only say f'(x)>0 for one interval. Sort out wetin you fit talk for sure from dis information alone.
l-m-h2-b0d04-12.s.s1.prompt: Wetin we fit know from di sign of di derivative alone?
l-m-h2-b0d04-12.s.s1.o.a: Di minimum value of f for di interval na 0
l-m-h2-b0d04-12.s.s1.r.a: Di sign of di derivative alone no fit decide di minimum value.
l-m-h2-b0d04-12.s.s1.o.b: Di graph of f for di interval dey convex downward
l-m-h2-b0d04-12.s.s1.r.b: Di direction wey e dey curve depend on whether di derivative dey increase or decrease.
l-m-h2-b0d04-12.s.s1.o.c: Di values of f(x) for di interval positive
l-m-h2-b0d04-12.s.s1.r.c: f'(x)>0 na information about di slope. We no know di sign of di function values.
l-m-h2-b0d04-12.s.s1.o.d: f dey increase for di interval
l-m-h2-b0d04-12.s.s1.explain: If f'(x)>0, di slope of di tangent line positive, so f dey increase. We must know di sign of di function values and di direction of curving separately.
l-m-h2-b0d04-12.s.s2.model.0: f'(x)>0 mean say di slope of di tangent line positive, so di only thing we fit talk for sure na say f dey increase for di interval.
l-m-h2-b0d04-12.s.s2.model.1: Whether di function values positive na information about di position of f, wey we no fit know from di derivative alone, so na only di increase dem fix.

l-m-h2-b0d04-22.title: Wetin we need to fix one single indefinite integral?
l-m-h2-b0d04-22.goal: Find out which criterion (information) we really need to find indefinite integral F(x) of f(x)=2x, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d04-22.material: One indefinite integral of f(x)=2x na x²+C. We wan fix only one function F(x) among dem. Think about which information go help us know C.
l-m-h2-b0d04-22.s.s1.prompt: Which information we really need to know C?
l-m-h2-b0d04-22.s.s1.r.a: We don already know dis one, so C still no dey fixed.
l-m-h2-b0d04-22.s.s1.o.b: Say di domain of f na all real numbers
l-m-h2-b0d04-22.s.s1.r.b: Di domain no get anything to do with C.
l-m-h2-b0d04-22.s.s1.r.c: Di value of f no tell us C. We need value of F.
l-m-h2-b0d04-22.s.s1.o.d: Value for one point, for example F(1)=4
l-m-h2-b0d04-22.s.s1.explain: If F(1)=4, then 1+C=4, so C=3. Functions wey get di same derivative differ by one constant, so we need one value.
l-m-h2-b0d04-22.s.s2.model.0: F'(x)=2x dey di same no matter wetin C be, so e no fit decide C. Na only when we get value for one point like F(1)=4 we go get C=3.
l-m-h2-b0d04-22.s.s2.model.1: Indefinite integral na family of functions wey differ by constants, so to pick one of dem we need function value F(a) for one point.

l-m-h2-b0d05-06.title: Permutation or combination: wetin we suppose look?
l-m-h2-b0d05-06.material: Choose 3 from 8 club candidates. Think about wetin to check so you fit decide whether to count di number of cases with permutations or combinations.
l-m-h2-b0d05-06.s.s1.o.a: Which day of di month di selection dey
l-m-h2-b0d05-06.s.s1.r.a: Di date no be criterion wey dey separate permutations from combinations.
l-m-h2-b0d05-06.s.s1.o.b: Di age order of di candidates
l-m-h2-b0d05-06.s.s1.r.b: Age order no be order wey depend on how dem choose dem, so e no fit be di criterion.
l-m-h2-b0d05-06.s.s1.o.c: Di name lengths of di 8 candidates
l-m-h2-b0d05-06.s.s1.r.c: Name length no get anything to do with how dem dey count di number of cases.
l-m-h2-b0d05-06.s.s1.o.d: Whether di people wey dem choose go do different roles
l-m-h2-b0d05-06.s.s1.explain: Even for di same 3 people, count with permutations, wey dey separate order, if di roles different, and with combinations if di roles dey same.
l-m-h2-b0d05-06.s.s2.model.0: You need to know whether di 3 people wey dem choose get different roles. If di roles different, order matter, so na permutation.
l-m-h2-b0d05-06.s.s2.model.1: If di roles dey same, di same 3 people count as one way, so na combination; if dem different, each order different, so na permutation. Age and date no matter.

l-m-h2-b0d05-07.title: Wetin dem need to find P(A|B)?
l-m-h2-b0d05-07.goal: Find out which criterion (information) dem must get to find di conditional probability P(A|B), and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d05-07.material: Two events A and B dey, and we know say B don happen. We wan find P(A|B), di probability say A go happen. Think about which probabilities we need to know so di value go dey determined.
l-m-h2-b0d05-07.s.s1.prompt: Which information dem must get to determine P(A|B)?
l-m-h2-b0d05-07.s.s1.r.b: With just dis two probabilities, we no know di overlap P(A∩B), so di value no dey determined.
l-m-h2-b0d05-07.s.s1.r.c: Di probability of di union alone no tell us di proportion of A inside B.
l-m-h2-b0d05-07.s.s1.o.d: P(A) wit P(di complement of A)
l-m-h2-b0d05-07.s.s1.r.d: Di two values add reach 1, so dem no give new information and dem no get anything to do with B.
l-m-h2-b0d05-07.s.s1.explain: P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B). We need to know how much A overlap with B and di size of B.
l-m-h2-b0d05-07.s.s2.model.0: P(A|B) na P(A∩B) divided by P(B), so dem must get dis two probabilities. With just P(A) and P(B) we no know di overlap.
l-m-h2-b0d05-07.s.s2.model.1: Na di proportion of di cases wey B happen and A too happen, so we need di probability of di overlap and di probability of B. Di union alone no do.

l-m-h2-b0d05-08.title: Wetin we suppose check to talk say na binomial distribution?
l-m-h2-b0d05-08.goal: Find out which criterion (information) dem must get to know whether random variable follow binomial distribution, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d05-08.material: We wan check whether we fit talk say random variable X follow binomial distribution B(n, p). Think about which conditions dem need to check.
l-m-h2-b0d05-08.s.s1.o.a: Fixed number of trials, independent, constant probability of success
l-m-h2-b0d05-08.s.s1.o.b: Di probability of success dey always 0.5?
l-m-h2-b0d05-08.s.s1.r.b: p no need to be 0.5. E only need to be constant.
l-m-h2-b0d05-08.s.s1.o.c: Di number of trials na 10 or more?
l-m-h2-b0d05-08.s.s1.r.c: Di size of n no matter. E still be binomial distribution even with fewer than 10 trials.
l-m-h2-b0d05-08.s.s1.r.d: To be integer values alone no make am binomial distribution.
l-m-h2-b0d05-08.s.s1.explain: Na binomial distribution wen di number of trials dey fixed, each trial dey independent, and di probability of success dey di same.
l-m-h2-b0d05-08.s.s2.model.0: Binomial distribution hold wen di probability of success dey constant across independent trials of fixed number, so dem must check dis three things.
l-m-h2-b0d05-08.s.s2.model.1: p no need to be 0.5 and n no need to big, so just look di number of trials, independence, and constant probability of success. Integer results alone no do.

l-m-h2-b0d05-09.title: Wetin determine di length of confidence interval?
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.topic: Statistical estimation (how to estimate with statistics)
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.goal: Find out which criterion (information) dem must get to find di length of confidence interval, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.material: We build confidence interval for di population mean from sample wey dem draw from population wey we know di standard deviation. Think about which information determine how long di interval go be.
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.s.s1.prompt: Choose di information wey determine di length of di interval.
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.s.s1.o.a: Confidence level, population standard deviation, sample size
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.s.s1.o.b: Di true value of di population mean
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.s.s1.r.b: Nobody sabi di true value, and e no get anything to do with how long di interval be.
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.s.s1.o.c: Di order wey dem take pick di sample
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.s.s1.r.c: Di order wey dem take pick am no dey change di sample mean or how long di interval be.
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.s.s1.o.d: Di value of di sample mean
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.s.s1.r.d: Di sample mean dey only move di center of di interval, e no dey change how long e be.
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.s.s1.explain: Di length na 2×(value for di confidence level)×σ/√n wey determine am. Di sample mean dey only decide di center of di interval.
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.s.s2.model.0: Di coefficient for di confidence level, σ, and di sample size n dey determine di length, so dem need all three. Di sample mean dey only decide di center.
l-m-h2-b0d05-09.s.s2.model.1: Even if di sample mean change, di whole interval just dey move, so di length no go change. Di confidence level, σ, and n dey decide di width.

l-m-h2-b0d05-10.title: Wetin we go do to standardize one normal distribution probability?
l-m-h2-b0d05-10.goal: Find out which criterion (information) dem must get to find di value of P(X≥a) for one normal distribution N(m, σ²), and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d05-10.material: When random variable X follow di normal distribution N(m, σ²), we wan find P(X≥a) with di standard normal table. Think about which values dem must get to standardize.
l-m-h2-b0d05-10.s.s1.prompt: Choose di information wey dem need.
l-m-h2-b0d05-10.s.s1.r.a: If σ no dey, we no fit know how many σ a dey away from di mean.
l-m-h2-b0d05-10.s.s1.r.b: If di mean m no dey, we no fit know whether a big pass di mean or small pass di mean.
l-m-h2-b0d05-10.s.s1.r.c: Dem no dey use di sample size to standardize; dem need m and σ.
l-m-h2-b0d05-10.s.s1.o.d: Di three values m, σ, and a
l-m-h2-b0d05-10.s.s1.explain: We dey standardize with Z=(X-m)/σ, so dem need m and σ, and dem need di reference value a wey we dey find too.
l-m-h2-b0d05-10.s.s2.model.0: We must change am to Z=(a-m)/σ, so dem need di mean m, di standard deviation σ, and di reference value a, all of dem. If even one no dey, we no fit find Z.
l-m-h2-b0d05-10.s.s2.model.1: If na only m dey, we no fit divide by σ, and if na only σ dey, we no fit subtract di mean, so dem must give all three values before we fit standardize.

l-m-h2-b0d06-06.title: When we fit use mathematical probability?
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.goal: To know di condition for using mathematical probability n(A)/n(S), decide which criterion (information) dem really need, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.material: We wan find di probability of event A as n(A)/n(S), na so to say, 'di ratio of di numbers of cases'. Think about which condition dem need before dem allow dis method.
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.s.s1.prompt: Choose di condition wey dem really need.
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.s.s1.o.a: Dem repeat di trial many times.
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.s.s1.r.a: Di number of repetitions no get anything to do with di ratio of cases. Di outcomes must dey equally likely.
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.s.s1.o.b: Each outcome get equal chance to happen.
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.s.s1.o.c: All di outcomes come out as numbers.
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.s.s1.r.c: E no matter whether di outcomes na numbers. Wetin matter na whether dem equally likely.
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.s.s1.r.d: To get few kinds of outcomes no mean say dem equally likely.
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.s.s1.explain: Wen every outcome equally likely, di ratio of di numbers of cases go be di probability. If one side dey come up pass, you no fit use am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.s.s2.model.0: Di ratio of di numbers of cases go be di probability only wen all outcomes equally likely, so dem need dat condition. Di number of repetitions no matter.
l-m-h2-b0d06-06.s.s2.model.1: If some face dey come up pass, like bent die, we no fit find di probability from di ratio of di numbers of faces, so di outcomes must dey equally likely.

l-m-h2-b0d06-07.title: How to decide di type by looking at order and repetition
l-m-h2-b0d06-07.goal: To know di type of counting for choosing 4 drinks, decide which criterion (information) dem really need, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-07.material: 3 kinds of drinks dey, and you fit choose di same kind more than once. We wan count di ways to choose 4 drinks. Di order of choosing no matter. Decide di type by looking at di order and whether dem allow repetition.
l-m-h2-b0d06-07.s.s1.r.a: You no fit pick 4 items from 3 kinds without overlap. Repetition too no fit.
l-m-h2-b0d06-07.s.s1.r.b: Dis type dey separate order, so e different from dis problem, where order no matter.
l-m-h2-b0d06-07.s.s1.r.c: E no allow repetition, so you no fit choose di same drink two times.
l-m-h2-b0d06-07.s.s1.explain: Order no matter and dem fit choose di same kind many times, so na combination with repetition: 3H4=6C4=15 ways.
l-m-h2-b0d06-07.s.s2.model.0: Order no matter, so e belong to di combination family, and dem fit choose di same kind many times, so na combination with repetition 3H4.
l-m-h2-b0d06-07.s.s2.model.1: If dem allow repetition, di combination 3C4 no fit work, and as order no matter, e no be permutation with repetition, wey dey separate order. So na combination with repetition.

l-m-h2-b0d06-08.title: Probability say at least one spoil: wetin we need?
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.topic: Addition rule of probability and complementary events
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.goal: To know di probability say at least one spoil, decide which criterion (information) dem really need, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.material: Di probability say one product spoil na 0.1, and di products no depend on each other. We wan find di probability say at least 1 of 5 products spoil. Think about which probability enough to know.
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.s.s1.prompt: Which probability go settle di answer di easiest way?
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.s.s1.o.a: Di probability say all 5 dey normal
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.s.s1.o.b: Only di probability say exactly 1 spoil
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.s.s1.r.b: "At least 1" include 2 or more too, so dis one alone no enough.
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.s.s1.r.c: Di price no get anything to do with di probability say e spoil.
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.s.s1.r.d: Na only di case wey all spoil, so di cases wey only some spoil no dey inside.
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.s.s1.explain: Di complement of 'at least 1 spoil' na 'all normal'. Di answer na 1-(0.9)⁵.
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.s.s2.model.0: Di complement of 'at least 1 spoil' na 'all 5 normal', so if you know dat probability 0.9⁵, you go subtract am from 1 to get di answer.
l-m-h2-b0d06-08.s.s2.model.1: To subtract di case wey all dey normal simple pass to add di cases of 1, 2, ..., 5 spoil one by one, so dem need dat probability.

l-m-h2-b0d06-09.title: Wetin make sample represent di population well?
l-m-h2-b0d06-09.goal: To know di standard for sample wey represent di population well, decide which criterion (information) dem really need, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-09.material: For one school wey get 1200 students, dem choose 100 students to survey di average daily sleep time. Think about how dem suppose choose di students so di sample go represent all di students well.
l-m-h2-b0d06-09.s.s1.r.a: Students wey volunteer fit get particular tendency, so di sample lean to one side.
l-m-h2-b0d06-09.s.s1.o.b: Make every student get equal chance to dem choose am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-09.s.s1.o.c: Choose all di students of one class.
l-m-h2-b0d06-09.s.s1.r.c: One class fit different from di whole school, so di sample lean to one side.
l-m-h2-b0d06-09.s.s1.o.d: Choose di first 100 students wey respond.
l-m-h2-b0d06-09.s.s1.r.d: If dem only gather students wey respond quick, di sample fit lean to one side.
l-m-h2-b0d06-09.s.s1.explain: E must be random sampling, where every student get equal chance to dem choose am, so di sample no go lean to one side.
l-m-h2-b0d06-09.s.s2.model.0: Every student must get equal chance to dem choose am so dem no go gather only particular students, and then di sample go represent di population well.
l-m-h2-b0d06-09.s.s2.model.1: Volunteers or students wey respond first fit get similar tendencies, so dem must choose dem at random so di sample no go lean to one side.

l-m-h2-b0d01-07.title: When x increase by 1, how y dey change?
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.goal: From several examples of change for exponential function wey dem show for table, find and talk the rule, then check the rule with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.material: One function dey wey y=3, 6, 12, 24 when x=0, 1, 2, 3. We wan find the rule for this table.
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.s.s1.prompt: Which rule you fit read from the table?
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.s.s1.o.a: Every time x increase by 1, y increase by 3
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.s.s1.r.a: The first increase na 3, but the next ones na 6 and 12, wey different.
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.s.s1.o.b: Every time x increase by 1, y become 2 times as big
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.s.s1.o.c: y dey directly proportional to x
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.s.s1.r.c: When x=0, y=3, so e no pass through the origin.
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.s.s1.o.d: Every time x increase by 1, y increase by 2
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.s.s1.r.d: The amounts of increase na 3, 6, and 12, so dem no be constant 2.
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.s.s1.explain: 6÷3, 12÷6, and 24÷12 all na 2. When x increase by 1, y become 2 times as big, so y=3·2ˣ.
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.s.s2.model.0: 6÷3, 12÷6, and 24÷12 all na 2, so when x increase by 1, y become 2 times as big, and we fit talk say y=3·2ˣ.
l-m-h2-b0d01-07.s.s2.model.1: The amounts of increase na 3, 6, and 12, wey no constant, but the ratio always na 2, so this na the rule of exponential function.

l-m-h2-b0d01-17.title: How to find di period of cos3x from a table
l-m-h2-b0d01-17.goal: From plenty examples of di period of y=cos3x, find di rule and talk am, then check di rule with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d01-17.material: We find di values of y=cos3x for x=0, π/6, π/3, π/2, 2π/3 and we get 1, 0, −1, 0, 1. We wan guess di period from dis table.
l-m-h2-b0d01-17.s.s1.prompt: Which period fit dem guess from di table?
l-m-h2-b0d01-17.s.s1.r.a: For x=π/3, y=−1, so e never return to di first value, 1.
l-m-h2-b0d01-17.s.s1.r.b: For x=π/2, y=0, so e never return to di first value.
l-m-h2-b0d01-17.s.s1.r.d: 2π no be di basic period, na distance wey cover plenty repeats.
l-m-h2-b0d01-17.s.s1.explain: For x=2π/3, y=1 for di first time. E match di period formula 2π/|3|=2π/3.
l-m-h2-b0d01-17.s.s2.model.0: For x=0, y=1, and y na 1 again for di first time for x=2π/3, so we guess say di period na 2π/3.
l-m-h2-b0d01-17.s.s2.model.1: y go 1, 0, −1, 0, 1, wey be one full up-and-down inside 2π/3, so di period na 2π/3. E also match 2π÷3.

l-m-h2-b0d01-26.title: Sums of two terms wey dia numbers add reach di same value
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.goal: From plenty examples of rules between di terms of an arithmetic sequence, find di rule and talk am, then check di rule with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.material: For di arithmetic sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 27, a₂+a₆=30, a₃+a₅=30, and a₁+a₇=30. We wan find di rule inside dis example.
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di rule wey dem find inside di examples?
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.s.s1.o.a: Two terms wey dia numbers differ by di same amount get di same sum
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.s.s1.r.a: a₂+a₃=18 and a₄+a₅=34, wey no be di same.
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.s.s1.o.b: Terms for odd positions always get di same sum
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.s.s1.r.b: a₁+a₃=14 and a₃+a₅=30, wey no be di same.
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.s.s1.o.c: Two terms wey dia numbers add reach di same value get di same sum
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.s.s1.o.d: If you add any two terms, di sum go be 30
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.s.s1.r.d: Cases dey wey no be 30, like a₁+a₂=10.
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.s.s1.explain: All the pairs wey their term numbers add reach the same 8 get sum of 30. Di common difference no dey change, so when one side go up, di other side go come down.
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.s.s2.model.0: a₂+a₆, a₃+a₅, and a₁+a₇ all get number sum of 8 and sum of 30, so we fit talk say if di number sums equal, di sums of di terms go equal too.
l-m-h2-b0d01-26.s.s2.model.1: Di terms dey grow by di common difference 4 every time, so if di number go up 1 for one side and come down 1 for di other side, di sum no dey change.

l-m-h2-b0d01-30.title: How to Find Pattern for Sum of Fractions
l-m-h2-b0d01-30.goal: Look for pattern inside several cases of di sum of di first n terms, talk di pattern, and check am with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d01-30.material: Make Sₙ be di sum of di first n terms of di sequence wey im terms be 1/(1·2), 1/(2·3), 1/(3·4), …. Then S₁=1/2, S₂=2/3, S₃=3/4, S₄=4/5.
l-m-h2-b0d01-30.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be Sₙ, as you guess am from di cases?
l-m-h2-b0d01-30.s.s1.explain: If you write 1/(k(k+1))=1/k−1/(k+1), di middle terms go cancel, so Sₙ=1−1/(n+1)=n/(n+1).
l-m-h2-b0d01-30.s.s2.model.0: From S₁=1/2, S₂=2/3, S₃=3/4, S₄=4/5, di numerator na n and di denominator na n+1, so we guess say Sₙ=n/(n+1).
l-m-h2-b0d01-30.s.s2.model.1: Since di denominator na n+1 and di numerator na n, we expect 5/6 for n=5, and true true 4/5+1/30=5/6, so di pattern correct.

l-m-h2-b0d01-35.title: How to Guess di General Term from di First Terms of a Recurrence
l-m-h2-b0d01-35.goal: Look for pattern inside several cases of di general term of a sequence wey recurrence define, talk di pattern, and check am with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d01-35.material: Di first four terms of di sequence wey a₁=1, aₙ₊₁=aₙ+2n+1 define na 1, 4, 9, 16. We wan guess di general term and then check am by mathematical induction.
l-m-h2-b0d01-35.s.s1.prompt: Which guess fit make we check am by induction?
l-m-h2-b0d01-35.s.s1.r.a: a₂=3, but di real a₂ na 4.
l-m-h2-b0d01-35.s.s1.r.b: a₂=2, but di real a₂ na 4.
l-m-h2-b0d01-35.s.s1.r.c: a₃=7, but di real a₃ na 9.
l-m-h2-b0d01-35.s.s1.explain: 1, 4, 9, 16 na 1², 2², 3², 4². If aₙ=n², then n²+2n+1=(n+1)², so di recurrence hold too.
l-m-h2-b0d01-35.s.s2.model.0: 1, 4, 9, 16 na 1², 2², 3², 4², so we guess say aₙ=n². Di recurrence fit too, since n²+2n+1=(n+1)².
l-m-h2-b0d01-35.s.s2.model.1: Since aₙ₊₁−aₙ na di odd numbers 3, 5, 7 wey dey grow, di square numbers 1, 4, 9, 16 follow, so we fit see say aₙ=n².

l-m-h2-b0d02-07.title: Where the Value of 2ˣ+1 Dey Go as x Dey Small?
l-m-h2-b0d02-07.goal: Look for pattern across several cases of how y=2ˣ+1 dey change as x dey small, talk the pattern, then check am with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d02-07.material: For y=2ˣ+1, when x=−1, −2, −3, −4, y na 1.5, 1.25, 1.125, 1.0625. We wan find pattern for these cases.
l-m-h2-b0d02-07.s.s1.o.a: As x dey small, y go big pass 1.5
l-m-h2-b0d02-07.s.s1.o.b: As x dey small, y dey get close to 1 without end
l-m-h2-b0d02-07.s.s1.o.c: As x dey small, y dey get close to 0
l-m-h2-b0d02-07.s.s1.r.c: y no dey go below 1, like 1.0625. E dey get close to 1.
l-m-h2-b0d02-07.s.s1.o.d: As x dey small, y go become negative
l-m-h2-b0d02-07.s.s1.r.d: 2ˣ always positive, so y big pass 1.
l-m-h2-b0d02-07.s.s1.explain: y−1 dey halve each time: 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625. y=1 na the asymptote.
l-m-h2-b0d02-07.s.s2.model.0: Since y−1 dey halve each time, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625, y dey get close to 1 without end, and because 2ˣ>0, e no dey ever really become 1.
l-m-h2-b0d02-07.s.s2.model.1: Each time x reduce by 1, 2ˣ dey halve, so y=2ˣ+1 no dey go below 1 but e dey get close to 1, and the asymptote na y=1.

l-m-h2-b0d02-16.goal: Look for pattern inside several cases of di relationship between a side and di sine of di angle wey face am, talk di pattern, and check am with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d02-16.material: For triangles wey dey inside a circle wey get diameter 5, dem measure side a and di angle A wey face am. (a, sinA) na (3, 0.6), (4, 0.8), (5, 1). We wan find pattern for dis cases.
l-m-h2-b0d02-16.s.s1.o.a: Di value of a−sinA always dey di same
l-m-h2-b0d02-16.s.s1.o.b: Di value of a×sinA always dey di same
l-m-h2-b0d02-16.s.s1.o.c: sinA always na half of a
l-m-h2-b0d02-16.s.s1.r.c: 0.6 no be half of 3; na 1/5 of am.
l-m-h2-b0d02-16.s.s1.o.d: Di value of a÷sinA always na 5
l-m-h2-b0d02-16.s.s1.explain: 3÷0.6, 4÷0.8, and 5÷1 all na 5, e equal di diameter of di circle. Dis na di law of sines, a/sinA=2R.
l-m-h2-b0d02-16.s.s2.model.0: 3÷0.6, 4÷0.8, and 5÷1 all na 5, so a÷sinA no dey change, and dis value equal di circle diameter, 5.
l-m-h2-b0d02-16.s.s2.model.1: For di law of sines a/sinA=2R, 2R=5, so a/sinA na 5 for every side.

l-m-h2-b0d02-27.title: How to find di pattern for di sum of di first n terms
l-m-h2-b0d02-27.goal: Find one pattern from plenty cases of di sum of di first n terms of a geometric sequence, talk am, and check am with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d02-27.material: Make Sₙ be di sum of di first n terms of a geometric sequence wey get first term 1 and common ratio 2. S₁=1, S₂=3, S₃=7, S₄=15. We wan find one pattern from dis cases.
l-m-h2-b0d02-27.s.s1.r.b: S₁ go be 2, wey no be di same as di real 1.
l-m-h2-b0d02-27.s.s1.r.c: S₃ go be 9, wey no be di same as di real 7.
l-m-h2-b0d02-27.s.s1.r.d: S₃ go be 5, wey no be di same as di real 7.
l-m-h2-b0d02-27.s.s1.explain: If you add 1 to 1, 3, 7, 15, you go get 2, 4, 8, 16. So Sₙ=2ⁿ−1.
l-m-h2-b0d02-27.s.s2.model.0: If you add 1 to S₁ reach S₄, you go get 2, 4, 8, 16, wey be powers of 2, so we guess say Sₙ=2ⁿ−1.
l-m-h2-b0d02-27.s.s2.model.1: Di sums 1, 3, 7, 15 each na 1 less than 2, 4, 8, 16, so Sₙ=2ⁿ−1, wey also match di formula (2ⁿ−1)/(2−1).

l-m-h2-b0d02-35.goal: Find pattern from several cases of di sum of products of two consecutive numbers, talk am, and check am with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d02-35.material: Make Sₙ=1·2+2·3+3·4+…+n(n+1). S₁=2, S₂=8, S₃=20, S₄=40. We wan guess di general formula and check am by induction.
l-m-h2-b0d02-35.s.s1.r.a: S₁ for be 1, wey different from di real 2.
l-m-h2-b0d02-35.s.s1.r.b: S₁ for be 1, wey different from di real 2.
l-m-h2-b0d02-35.s.s1.r.c: S₂ for be 3, wey different from di real 8.

l-m-h2-b0d02-35.s.s2.model.1: Because e be di product of three consecutive numbers wey dem divide by 3, for n=5 we expect 5·6·7/3=70, and true true S₄+5·6=70, so e correct.

l-m-h2-b0d03-03.title: To put x=10, 100, 1000
l-m-h2-b0d03-03.goal: Find pattern from several cases of di values of (3x²+x)/(x²−5) as x→∞, talk am, and check am with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d03-03.material: If you put x=10, 100, 1000 inside f(x)=(3x²+x)/(x²−5), f(x) go be about 3.263, 3.012, 3.001. Find di value wey f(x) dey near as x dey grow without end.
l-m-h2-b0d03-03.s.s1.prompt: Which value f(x) dey near as x→∞?
l-m-h2-b0d03-03.s.s1.r.a: Di values no dey grow; dem settle for 3.001.
l-m-h2-b0d03-03.s.s1.r.b: Na di value from looking only di coefficient of di denominator x². Di values for di table near 3.
l-m-h2-b0d03-03.s.s1.r.c: Di values dey reduce but dem no go reach 0; dem stop near 3.
l-m-h2-b0d03-03.s.s1.explain: Di values 3.263, 3.012, 3.001 dey near 3. This one match di ratio of di highest-degree coefficients, 3/1, too.
l-m-h2-b0d03-03.s.s2.model.0: As x dey grow, di values dey reduce as 3.263, 3.012, 3.001 and dem near 3, so we fit talk say di limit na 3.
l-m-h2-b0d03-03.s.s2.model.1: Di ratio of di highest-degree coefficients 3 and 1 na 3, and di values for di table dey near 3, so di pattern say e na 3 correct.

l-m-h2-b0d03-10.title: To find pattern for the limit of (xⁿ−2ⁿ)/(x−2)
l-m-h2-b0d03-10.goal: Find pattern from several cases of the limit of (xⁿ−2ⁿ)/(x−2) as x→2, talk am, then check am with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d03-10.material: The limit of (xⁿ−2ⁿ)/(x−2) as x→2 na 4 for n=2, 12 for n=3, and 32 for n=4. Find pattern for these values and predict the value for n=5.
l-m-h2-b0d03-10.s.s1.prompt: Which one na the most suitable value for n=5?
l-m-h2-b0d03-10.s.s1.r.a: E just add 8 to 32. Na guess wey no check the pattern.
l-m-h2-b0d03-10.s.s1.r.b: Na guess wey add 20 follow the differences 8 and 20. E no match the pattern.
l-m-h2-b0d03-10.s.s1.r.c: E double the previous value. 4, 12, 32 no dey double each time.
l-m-h2-b0d03-10.s.s1.explain: The value na n·2ⁿ⁻¹ (2·2, 3·4, 4·8). For n=5, e be 5·16=80.
l-m-h2-b0d03-10.s.s2.model.0: 4=2·2, 12=3·4, 32=4·8, so the pattern n·2ⁿ⁻¹ show, and for n=5 e be 5·16=80.
l-m-h2-b0d03-10.s.s2.model.1: If you write each value as the product of n and one power of 2, the pattern fit, so for n=5 e be 5×2⁴=80.

l-m-h2-b0d03-14.goal: Find pattern from several cases of the rate of change of f(x)=x³ near x=2, talk am, then check am with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d03-14.material: For f(x)=x³, the average rate of change from x=2 to 2+h na 19 for h=1, 12.61 for h=0.1, and 12.0601 for h=0.01. Find the value wey e dey approach as h small more.
l-m-h2-b0d03-14.s.s1.prompt: Which value the average rate of change dey approach as h→0?
l-m-h2-b0d03-14.s.s1.r.a: Dem calculate am as 3·2. The rate of change of x³ na 3x², so e be 12.
l-m-h2-b0d03-14.s.s1.r.c: E round 12.61 up. The values dey keep reducing and dey approach 12.
l-m-h2-b0d03-14.s.s1.r.d: This na the very first value. The value dey change as h small.
l-m-h2-b0d03-14.s.s1.explain: E dey approach 12, like 12.61 and 12.0601. This equal f'(2)=3·2²=12.
l-m-h2-b0d03-14.s.s2.model.0: With h=1, 0.1, 0.01 the values dey shrink to 19, 12.61, 12.0601 and dey get close to 12, so the limit na 12.
l-m-h2-b0d03-14.s.s2.model.1: The differences from 12 dey keep small, like 0.61 and 0.0601, so the limit of the average rate of change na 12.

l-m-h2-b0d03-24.s.s2.model.0: 0.5, 2, and 4.5 na half of 1, 4, and 9, so di rule na a²/2, and when a=4 e na 8.
l-m-h2-b0d03-24.s.s2.model.1: Di value always equal di square of a divided by 2, so when a=4 we predict 16÷2=8.

l-m-h2-b0d04-03.material: [x] na di greatest integer wey no big pass x. As x→0.5 di limit na 0, and as x→1.5 di limit na 1. As x→2 di left side na 1 and di right side na 2, so limit no dey, and as x→3 di left side na 2 and di right side na 3, so limit no dey too.

l-m-h2-b0d04-03.s.s1.r.c: E no be integer, and di limit dey and e na 7.

l-m-h2-b0d04-03.s.s2.model.1: For di cases, di points wey no get limit na integers, like 2 and 3, so by di same rule limit no dey for a=4 too.

l-m-h2-b0d04-10.title: How to find di product rule for derivatives from cases
l-m-h2-b0d04-10.goal: Find and talk di rule from several cases of di derivative of a product f(x)g(x) of two functions, then check di rule with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d04-10.material: (x·x)'=2x, (x·x²)'=3x², (x²·x³)'=5x⁴. For each case, calculate f'g, fg', and so on, to find di rule for di derivative of di product fg.
l-m-h2-b0d04-10.s.s1.prompt: Which one na di correct rule?
l-m-h2-b0d04-10.s.s1.r.a: For x·x², f'g'=2x, but di real result na 3x².
l-m-h2-b0d04-10.s.s1.r.c: For x·x, x−x=0, but di real result na 2x.
l-m-h2-b0d04-10.s.s1.r.d: For x·x, 1+1=2, but di real result na 2x.
l-m-h2-b0d04-10.s.s1.explain: For x·x², f'g+fg'=x²+2x²=3x², and so on; all three cases fit. Di other rules fail for one case.
l-m-h2-b0d04-10.s.s2.model.0: If you calculate f'g+fg' for all three cases you get 2x, 3x², and 5x⁴, so we fit talk say di derivative of a product na f'g+fg'.
l-m-h2-b0d04-10.s.s2.model.1: f'g' or f'+g' give 2x or 1+2x for x·x², wey different from 3x², so na only f'g+fg' fit di cases.

l-m-h2-b0d04-19.goal: Find pattern from several cases of x wey function f(x)=x³−px get extremum, talk am, then check di pattern with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d04-19.material: For f(x)=x³−px, e get extrema for x=±1 when p=3, for x=±2 when p=12, and for x=±3 when p=27. Find pattern from dis cases and predict di x wey e go get extrema when p=48.
l-m-h2-b0d04-19.s.s1.prompt: Which one na di correct x for p=48?
l-m-h2-b0d04-19.s.s1.r.b: Dem look am as p÷4. E no match ±1 when p=3.
l-m-h2-b0d04-19.s.s1.r.c: Dem calculate 48÷3. When p=12 dis one give ±4, wey no be di same as di case.
l-m-h2-b0d04-19.s.s1.r.d: Dem take square root of p. When p=3 e be ±√3, no be ±1.
l-m-h2-b0d04-19.s.s1.explain: Because f'(x)=3x²−p=0, x=±√(p/3). Di cases 3, 12, 27 match ±1, ±2, ±3, and p=48 give ±4.
l-m-h2-b0d04-19.s.s2.model.0: Di square roots of 1, 4, 9 (p divide by 3) na 1, 2, 3, so di pattern na ±√(p/3), and p=48 give ±4.
l-m-h2-b0d04-19.s.s2.model.1: Di p for di cases get di form 3·1², 3·2², 3·3², so we fit predict say x=±4 when p=48=3·4².

l-m-h2-b0d04-23.title: Wetin go happen to di definite integral if you swap di upper and lower limits?
l-m-h2-b0d04-23.goal: Find pattern from several cases of di value when dem swap di upper and lower limits of definite integral, talk am, then check di pattern with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d04-23.material: Di definite integral of x from 0 to 2 na 2, and from 2 to 0 e na −2. Di definite integral of x² from 0 to 3 na 9, and from 3 to 0 e na −9. Find pattern from dis cases and predict di value from 4 to 1 when di definite integral of f from 1 to 4 na 7.
l-m-h2-b0d04-23.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di value of di definite integral of f from 4 to 1?
l-m-h2-b0d04-23.s.s1.r.a: Dis one na di value wey dem take as reciprocal. For di cases, na only di sign dey change.
l-m-h2-b0d04-23.s.s1.r.c: Dem miss di cases wey swapping di upper and lower limits change di sign.
l-m-h2-b0d04-23.s.s1.r.d: Dis one na di value of adding di two integrals. For di cases, di sign of di value itself dey change.
l-m-h2-b0d04-23.s.s1.explain: When dem swap am, di size remain di same and only di sign flip: 2 and −2, 9 and −9. So di value from 4 to 1 na −7.
l-m-h2-b0d04-23.s.s2.model.0: Every time dem swap di upper and lower limits for di cases, di size dey di same and only di sign opposite, so di definite integral from 4 to 1 na −7.
l-m-h2-b0d04-23.s.s2.model.1: Because dem get opposite signs, like 2 and −2, 9 and −9, we predict −7, wey be di opposite of 7.

l-m-h2-b0d05-11.title: Wetin be di sum of all di coefficients of (1+x)ⁿ?
l-m-h2-b0d05-11.goal: Find and talk one pattern from plenty cases of di sum of di coefficients wen dem expand (1+x)ⁿ, then check di pattern with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d05-11.material: We expand (1+x)ⁿ and add all di coefficients: di sum na 2 for n=1, 4 for n=2, 8 for n=3, and 16 for n=4. Find di pattern for how di sum dey change as n dey grow.
l-m-h2-b0d05-11.s.s1.prompt: Which one be di correct pattern for di sum of coefficients?
l-m-h2-b0d05-11.s.s1.r.b: For n=3 e give 6, but di real one na 8, so e no fit.
l-m-h2-b0d05-11.s.s1.r.c: For n=2 e give 5, but di real one na 4, so e no fit.
l-m-h2-b0d05-11.s.s1.r.d: For n=1 e give 4, but di real one na 2, so e no fit.
l-m-h2-b0d05-11.s.s1.explain: Di sums 2, 4, 8, 16 dey become 2 times bigger each time. If you put x=1, e give di sum (1+1)ⁿ=2ⁿ.
l-m-h2-b0d05-11.s.s2.model.0: Di sum dey become 2 times bigger each time: 2, 4, 8, 16, so e na 2ⁿ. We fit check say n=5 suppose give 32.
l-m-h2-b0d05-11.s.s2.model.1: If you put 1 for x, e give di sum of di coefficients, and (1+1)ⁿ=2ⁿ, so every time n grow by 1, di sum dey become 2 times bigger.

l-m-h2-b0d05-12.title: Di number of ways to choose n from 3 kinds
l-m-h2-b0d05-12.goal: Find and talk one pattern from plenty cases of di number of ways to choose n from 3 different kinds, then check di pattern with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d05-12.material: Bread get 3 kinds, and you fit choose plenty of di same kind. Order no matter. Di number of ways to choose n breads na 3 for n=1, 6 for n=2, 10 for n=3, and 15 for n=4.
l-m-h2-b0d05-12.s.s1.prompt: Which one be di correct number of ways for n=5?
l-m-h2-b0d05-12.s.s1.r.a: Dem think say di difference na always 3. Di real differences na 3, 4, 5, dem dey grow by one each time.
l-m-h2-b0d05-12.s.s1.r.b: Dem add di last difference 5 as e be. Dem miss say di difference dey grow by one each time.
l-m-h2-b0d05-12.s.s1.r.d: Dem take am as n². For n=4 e give 16, wey no match di real 15.
l-m-h2-b0d05-12.s.s1.explain: Di amounts wey dem add na 3, 4, 5, dem dey grow by 1, so di next one na +6. 15+6=21, wey equal 7C2.
l-m-h2-b0d05-12.s.s2.model.0: Di amount wey dem add for each step grow by 1: 3, 4, 5. So di next one go add 6, and e give 15+6=21 ways.
l-m-h2-b0d05-12.s.s2.model.1: Di differences dey grow by one each time, so for n=5, dem add 6 to get 21. Dis value equal 7C2=21, so di pattern correct.

l-m-h2-b0d05-13.title: How to find pattern for di average number of bad items
l-m-h2-b0d05-13.goal: Find and talk one pattern from plenty cases of di mean of one binomial distribution, then check di pattern with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d05-13.material: We check n products wey get defect rate of 0.2 and we find di mean of di number of bad items X: 1 for n=5, 2 for n=10, 3 for n=15. We wan find one pattern and use am for other n.
l-m-h2-b0d05-13.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di mean number of bad items for n=40?
l-m-h2-b0d05-13.s.s1.r.a: Dem take am as n÷4. For n=5 e give 1.25, wey no be di real 1.
l-m-h2-b0d05-13.s.s1.r.b: Dem take am as n÷10. For n=10 e give 1, but di real one na 2.
l-m-h2-b0d05-13.s.s1.r.d: Dem take am as n-4. For n=10 e give 6, but di real one na 2.
l-m-h2-b0d05-13.s.s1.explain: Wen n grow by 5, di mean grow by 1, so di mean na 0.2 times n. For n=40 e na 8, wey equal np.
l-m-h2-b0d05-13.s.s2.model.0: For n=5, 10, 15 di means na 1, 2, 3, so di mean na n×0.2. So for n=40 e na 40×0.2=8.
l-m-h2-b0d05-13.s.s2.model.1: Each time n grow by 5, di mean grow by 1, so e na 1/5 times n. Dis value na di defect rate 0.2 times n, so e na 8.

l-m-h2-b0d05-14.title: One pattern for di probability say e no go ever happen
l-m-h2-b0d05-14.topic: Probability of independent trials (trials wey no depend on each other)
l-m-h2-b0d05-14.goal: Find and talk one pattern from plenty cases of di probability say one event no go ever happen for independent trials, then check di pattern with one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d05-14.material: Di probability say di event go happen for one trial na 1/3. Wen dem repeat am independently n times, di probability say e no go ever happen na 2/3 for n=1, 4/9 for n=2, and 8/27 for n=3.
l-m-h2-b0d05-14.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di pattern for di probability say e no happen for all n trials?
l-m-h2-b0d05-14.s.s1.r.a: If n=2, e for be 1/3, but di real value na 4/9, so e no fit.
l-m-h2-b0d05-14.s.s1.r.d: If n=2, e for be 1/3, but di real value na 4/9, so e no fit.
l-m-h2-b0d05-14.s.s1.r.c: If n=3, e for be 6/27, but di real value na 8/27, so e no fit.
l-m-h2-b0d05-14.s.s1.explain: Dem multiply di probability 2/3 say e no happen each time because di events independent, and e give (2/3)ⁿ. All three values fit.
l-m-h2-b0d05-14.s.s2.model.0: 2/3, 4/9, and 8/27 na 2/3 wey dem multiply 1, 2, and 3 times, so di rule na (2/3)ⁿ. Na because independent probabilities dey multiply.
l-m-h2-b0d05-14.s.s2.model.1: Each time n go up by 1, dem multiply di previous value by 2/3, so di rule na (2/3)ⁿ. Wen n=3 e na 8/27, so all three cases fit.

l-m-h2-b0d05-15.title: How di sample mean dey change as di sample dey big?
l-m-h2-b0d05-15.topic: Distribution of di sample mean (how di sample mean spread)
l-m-h2-b0d05-15.goal: Find one rule from plenty cases of di standard deviation of di sample mean, talk am, and check am for one new case.
l-m-h2-b0d05-15.material: Dem draw samples of size n from one population wey get standard deviation 12, and dem find di standard deviation of di sample mean. E be 6 wen n=4, 4 wen n=9, 3 wen n=16, and 2 wen n=36. Find di rule.
l-m-h2-b0d05-15.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di standard deviation of di sample mean wen n=100?
l-m-h2-b0d05-15.s.s1.r.a: Dem use 12÷n. Wen n=4 dat one give 3, but di real value na 6.
l-m-h2-b0d05-15.s.s1.r.b: Dem think say di value go stay di same wen n change. Di table show say e dey small as n dey grow.
l-m-h2-b0d05-15.s.s1.r.c: Dem use di value for n=16 as e be. As n dey big, di value go still small pass.
l-m-h2-b0d05-15.s.s1.explain: Di standard deviation na 12÷√n. By di rule say e dey cut half wen n become 4 times bigger, n=100 give 12÷10=1.2.
l-m-h2-b0d05-15.s.s2.model.0: 6, 4, 3, 2 na 12 wey dem divide by 2, 3, 4, 6, and dis divisors na √n, so e na 12÷√n. Wen n=100 e na 1.2.
l-m-h2-b0d05-15.s.s2.model.1: Wen n go from 4 to 16, 4 times bigger, di value cut half from 6 to 3, so e dey inversely proportional to √n. So wen n=100 e na 12÷10=1.2.

l-m-h2-b0d06-10.goal: Find and talk di rule from several cases of di number of ways n people fit sit for round table, and check dat rule with new case.
l-m-h2-b0d06-10.material: Count di ways n people fit sit round one round table. Arrangements wey turn di same if you rotate count as one way. For n=3 2 ways dey, for n=4 6 ways dey, and for n=5 24 ways dey.
l-m-h2-b0d06-10.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di number of ways wen n=7?
l-m-h2-b0d06-10.s.s1.r.a: I take am as n!. For n=3 dat one give 6, but di real number na 2.
l-m-h2-b0d06-10.s.s1.r.c: I take am as (n-2)!. For n=3 dat one give 1, but di real number na 2.
l-m-h2-b0d06-10.s.s1.r.d: I take am as n(n-1). For n=3 dat one give 6, but di real number na 2.
l-m-h2-b0d06-10.s.s1.explain: 2, 6, 24 na (n-1)!. E be like say you fix one person and line up di other n-1 people, so for 7 people na 6!=720.
l-m-h2-b0d06-10.s.s2.model.0: 2, 6, 24 na 2!, 3!, 4!, so di rule na (n-1)!. So for n=7 720 ways dey, wey be 6!=720.
l-m-h2-b0d06-10.s.s2.model.1: To fix one person seat be like say you line up di other n-1 people for row, so di number na (n-1)!, and for n=7 e na 720.

l-m-h2-b0d06-11.title: If we connect n points, how many segments go dey?
l-m-h2-b0d06-11.goal: Find and talk di rule from several cases of di number of segments wey connect n points to each other, and check dat rule with new case.
l-m-h2-b0d06-11.material: Mark n points for one circle and connect every pair of points. Di number of segments na 3 for 3 points, 6 for 4 points, 10 for 5 points, and 15 for 6 points. Find di rule from how di numbers dey grow.
l-m-h2-b0d06-11.s.s1.prompt: How many segments dey wen 9 points dey?
l-m-h2-b0d06-11.s.s1.r.a: I take am as n(n-1). For n=4 dat one give 12, but di real number na 6.
l-m-h2-b0d06-11.s.s1.r.b: I take am as n². For n=3 dat one give 9, but di real number na 3.
l-m-h2-b0d06-11.s.s1.r.c: Dis one miss by one step. Na di number of segments for 10 points.
l-m-h2-b0d06-11.s.s1.explain: Wen dem add one point, di new segments na one from di new point to each old point. For 9 points, 1+2+...+8=36.
l-m-h2-b0d06-11.s.s2.model.0: Every time dem add one point, di segments increase by di number of old points. So for 9 points, na 1+2+...+8=36 segments.
l-m-h2-b0d06-11.s.s2.model.1: To choose two points decide one segment, so di number na nC2=n(n-1)/2, and for n=9 e na 36. E match 3, 6, 10, 15 too.
