l-m-h2-b0d06-12.topic: Conditional probability (chance wey depend on something)
l-m-h2-b0d06-12.title: Di rule for conditional probability wen dem dey draw balls without replacement
l-m-h2-b0d06-12.goal: Find and talk di rule from several cases of di probability say di second ball na white if di first ball na white, and check dat rule with new case.
l-m-h2-b0d06-12.material: One bag get 10 balls, and w of dem na white. Dem draw one ball and no put am back, then dem draw another ball. If di first ball na white, di probability say di second one na white too na 1/9 for w=2, 3/9 for w=4, and 5/9 for w=6.
l-m-h2-b0d06-12.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di probability wen w=8?
l-m-h2-b0d06-12.s.s1.r.a: I take am as 8/10, like sampling with replacement. For w=2 dat one give 2/10, wey different from 1/9.
l-m-h2-b0d06-12.s.s1.r.b: I take di numerator as w. For w=2 dat one give 2/9, wey different from di real 1/9.
l-m-h2-b0d06-12.s.s1.r.c: I take di denominator as 10. For w=2 dat one give 1/10, wey different from di real 1/9.
l-m-h2-b0d06-12.s.s1.explain: If di first ball na white, 9 balls remain and w-1 of dem na white. Di probability na (w-1)/9, and for w=8 e na 7/9.
l-m-h2-b0d06-12.s.s2.model.0: 1/9, 3/9, 5/9 get numerator w-1 and denominator 9, so di rule na (w-1)/9. So for w=8 e na 7/9.
l-m-h2-b0d06-12.s.s2.model.1: If di first ball na white, di remaining 9 balls get w-1 white ones, so di probability na (w-1)/9, and for w=8 e na 7/9.

l-m-h2-b0d06-13.title: Di rule for variance for coin tossing
l-m-h2-b0d06-13.goal: Find and talk di rule from several cases of di variance of di number of heads wen dem toss coin n times, and check dat rule with new case.
l-m-h2-b0d06-13.material: We find di variance of X, di number of heads wen dem toss fair coin n times. E be 1 for n=4, 2 for n=8, and 3 for n=12. We wan find di rule and use am for other values of n.
l-m-h2-b0d06-13.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di variance of X wen n=40?
l-m-h2-b0d06-13.s.s1.r.a: I take am as n÷2. For n=4 dat one give 2, but di real variance na 1.
l-m-h2-b0d06-13.s.s1.r.b: I think say di variance equal n. For n=4 dat one give 4, wey different from di real 1.
l-m-h2-b0d06-13.s.s1.r.d: I take am as n÷8. For n=4 dat one give 0.5, but di real variance na 1.
l-m-h2-b0d06-13.s.s1.explain: Di variance na 1/4 of n. For di binomial distribution variance np(1-p), p=1/2 give n/4, so for n=40 e na 10.
l-m-h2-b0d06-13.s.s2.model.0: Every time n go up by 4, di variance go up by 1, so e be 1/4 times n. So for n=40 e na 10.
l-m-h2-b0d06-13.s.s2.model.1: For di variance np(1-p), p=1/2 give n×1/2×1/2=n/4, so 1, 2, 3 fit, and for n=40 e na 10.

l-m-h2-b0d01-03.title: About how many digits 2¹⁰⁰ get?
l-m-h2-b0d01-03.goal: Estimate di number of digits of 2¹⁰⁰ to decide di size or range wey fit, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h2-b0d01-03.material: We wan estimate how many digits 2¹⁰⁰ get without calculator. Wetin we know na only say 2¹⁰=1024.
l-m-h2-b0d01-03.s.s1.r.a: Dis one treat 2¹⁰ as 10². 1024 na about 10³.
l-m-h2-b0d01-03.s.s1.r.c: Dis one treat di number of digits as about half of di exponent. When you multiply, di number go big plenty.
l-m-h2-b0d01-03.s.s1.r.d: Dis one treat di number of digits as di same as di exponent 100.
l-m-h2-b0d01-03.s.s1.explain: 2¹⁰≈10³, so 2¹⁰⁰=(2¹⁰)¹⁰≈10³⁰. 1024 big pass 1000, so e get 31 digits.
l-m-h2-b0d01-03.s.s2.model.0: 2¹⁰=1024≈10³, so 2¹⁰⁰=(2¹⁰)¹⁰≈10³⁰. 1024 small big pass 1000, so we estimate say e be 31-digit number.
l-m-h2-b0d01-03.s.s2.model.1: Every time you multiply 2 for 10 times, di number turn about 1000 times bigger, so 100 times go give about 10³⁰, and 10³⁰ na 31-digit number.

l-m-h2-b0d01-08.title: Between which two integers log₂100 dey?
l-m-h2-b0d01-08.topic: To estimate the value of logarithm
l-m-h2-b0d01-08.goal: Estimate the size of log₂100 to decide one suitable size or range, then explain your reasons.
l-m-h2-b0d01-08.material: We wan estimate which two integers log₂100 dey between without calculator. Use the values of the powers of 2.
l-m-h2-b0d01-08.s.s1.prompt: Between which two integers log₂100 dey?
l-m-h2-b0d01-08.s.s1.r.a: 2⁶=64 still small pass 100, so log₂100 big pass 6.
l-m-h2-b0d01-08.s.s1.r.c: 2⁷=128 don already big pass 100, so log₂100 small pass 7.
l-m-h2-b0d01-08.s.s1.r.d: This no be 100 divided by 2. Logarithm mean exponent.
l-m-h2-b0d01-08.s.s1.explain: 2⁶=64 and 2⁷=128, and 64<100<128, so log₂100 dey between 6 and 7.
l-m-h2-b0d01-08.s.s2.model.0: 2⁶=64<100<128=2⁷, so the exponent, wey be the value of the logarithm, dey between 6 and 7.
l-m-h2-b0d01-08.s.s2.model.1: If you multiply 2 6 times e give 64, wey small pass 100, and if you multiply am 7 times e give 128, wey big pass 100, so log₂100 dey between 6 and 7.

l-m-h2-b0d01-15.title: For which quadrant angle of 3 radians dey?
l-m-h2-b0d01-15.goal: Estimate the quadrant where angle of 3 radians dey to decide one suitable size or range, then explain your reasons.
l-m-h2-b0d01-15.material: The size 3 of the angle na for radians. If we take π as about 3.14, we wan decide the quadrant where the terminal side of this angle dey.
l-m-h2-b0d01-15.s.s1.prompt: For which quadrant the terminal side of 3 radians dey?
l-m-h2-b0d01-15.s.s1.r.b: This one read 3 as about 3°. 3 big pass π/2≈1.57.
l-m-h2-b0d01-15.s.s1.r.c: 3 small pass π≈3.14, so e never reach Quadrant 3.
l-m-h2-b0d01-15.s.s1.explain: π/2≈1.57<3<π≈3.14, so the terminal side of 3 radians dey Quadrant 2.
l-m-h2-b0d01-15.s.s2.model.0: π/2≈1.57 and π≈3.14, so 3 dey between the two, wey mean Quadrant 2.
l-m-h2-b0d01-15.s.s2.model.1: 3 radians na about 172°, so we fit estimate say e dey between 90° and 180°, wey be Quadrant 2.

l-m-h2-b0d01-18.goal: Estimate di range of di maximum value of sin x + cos x so dat you go choose one correct size or range, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h2-b0d01-18.material: sin x and cos x each at least −1 and at most 1. We wan estimate inside which range di maximum value of dia sum sin x + cos x dey.
l-m-h2-b0d01-18.s.s1.prompt: Which one be di correct range for di maximum value?

l-m-h2-b0d01-18.s.s1.r.b: No x dey wey sin x=cos x=1, so e no fit be 2.
l-m-h2-b0d01-18.s.s1.r.c: Each one no fit pass 1, so di sum no fit pass 2.
l-m-h2-b0d01-18.s.s1.explain: For x=π/4 di sum na about 1.41, wey big pass 1, and di two no fit be 1 for di same time, so e small pass 2.

l-m-h2-b0d01-24.material: Two sides of a triangle na 4 and 7, and di included angle θ between dem fit change between 0° and 180°. We wan estimate di range wey di length of di third side c dey.
l-m-h2-b0d01-24.s.s1.prompt: Which one be di correct range for c?

l-m-h2-b0d01-24.s.s1.r.c: If θ small, c fit small pass 7.
l-m-h2-b0d01-24.s.s1.explain: For c²=65−56cosθ, cosθ dey between −1 and 1, so c² dey between 9 and 121, and c dey between 3 and 11.

l-m-h2-b0d02-03.title: How many half-lives dem need to drop below 1%?
l-m-h2-b0d02-03.goal: Estimate the number of half-lives for the amount to fall below 1%, decide one suitable size or range, then explain your reasons.
l-m-h2-b0d02-03.material: One substance dey reduce to half for amount with each half-life. We wan estimate how many half-lives must pass before e fall below 1% of the original amount.
l-m-h2-b0d02-03.s.s1.prompt: After how many half-lives e first fall below 1%?
l-m-h2-b0d02-03.s.s1.r.a: After 5, e be 1/32, about 3%, wey still pass 1%.
l-m-h2-b0d02-03.s.s1.r.c: After 7, e don be 1/128, so 10 pass wetin dem need.
l-m-h2-b0d02-03.s.s1.r.d: This estimate treat am like 100 divided by 2. E dey shrink by multiplying.
l-m-h2-b0d02-03.s.s1.explain: 2⁶=64, so 1/64≈1.6%, and 2⁷=128, so 1/128≈0.8%. After 7 times, e first fall below 1%.
l-m-h2-b0d02-03.s.s2.model.0: Since 2⁶=64, after 6 times e be 1/64≈1.6%, still at least 1%, and after 7 times e be 1/128≈0.8%, so dem need 7 times.
l-m-h2-b0d02-03.s.s2.model.1: If e halve each time, e give 1/2ⁿ, so we just need the smallest n wey 2ⁿ>100, and since 2⁷=128>100, the answer na 7 times.

l-m-h2-b0d02-12.title: With 7% Annual Compound Interest, How Many Years Before the Principal Become 2 Times?
l-m-h2-b0d02-12.goal: Estimate the time for the principal to become 2 times with compound interest, decide one suitable size or range, then explain your reasons.
l-m-h2-b0d02-12.material: One compound-interest deposit dey wey e principal dey grow by 7% every year. We wan estimate roughly how many years e go take for the principal to become 2 times.
l-m-h2-b0d02-12.s.s1.prompt: Which one na suitable time for am to become 2 times?
l-m-h2-b0d02-12.s.s1.r.a: 1.07⁵≈1.4 times, so e neva reach 2 times yet.
l-m-h2-b0d02-12.s.s1.r.c: Dis estimate come from say make you calculate 100÷7. For compound interest, interest dey earn interest too.
l-m-h2-b0d02-12.s.s1.r.d: 1.07²⁰≈3.9 times, so e don pass 2 times far before dat time.
l-m-h2-b0d02-12.s.s1.explain: 1.07¹⁰≈1.97 and 1.07¹¹≈2.10, so e go reach 2 times between 10 and 11 years.
l-m-h2-b0d02-12.s.s2.model.0: 1.07¹⁰≈1.97 neva reach 2 times, and 1.07¹¹≈2.10, so e go reach 2 times between 10 and 11 years.
l-m-h2-b0d02-12.s.s2.model.1: Because interest dey earn interest, e quick pass di 100÷7≈14 years wey simple interest go take, so we fit estimate say e go take small pass 10 years.

l-m-h2-b0d02-17.title: How Big sin 1 (Radian) Be?
l-m-h2-b0d02-17.goal: Estimate di size of sin1 (1 dey for radians), decide one size or range wey fit, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h2-b0d02-17.material: Di angle 1 dey for radians. We wan estimate di size of sin1 with π/4≈0.785, π/3≈1.047 and sin(π/4)≈0.71, sin(π/3)≈0.87.

l-m-h2-b0d03-04.material: Make f(x)=(√x−2)/(x−4); we wan estimate im value for x=4.01, wey near x=4 well well. When x near 4, both di numerator and di denominator dey near 0.

l-m-h2-b0d03-04.s.s1.r.c: Na di value from reading 1/(√x+2) upside down as a fraction.

l-m-h2-b0d03-04.s.s1.r.d: Di numerator and denominator both dey small together, so di ratio no be 0.
l-m-h2-b0d03-04.s.s1.explain: (√x−2)/(x−4)=1/(√x+2), so when x≈4 e be about 1/4. Di real f(4.01) na about 0.2498.
l-m-h2-b0d03-04.s.s2.model.0: Since x−4=(√x−2)(√x+2), if you cancel am e go give 1/(√x+2), and √4.01≈2.0025, so e be about 0.25.
l-m-h2-b0d03-04.s.s2.model.1: If you rationalize di numerator, e go give 1/(√x+2), so when x near 4 e be about 1/(2+2)=0.25.

l-m-h2-b0d03-19.goal: Estimate the height of thrown ball for e highest point to decide one suitable size or range, then explain your reasoning.
l-m-h2-b0d03-19.material: The height of the ball na h(t)=−t²+8t (m) (t seconds later, 0≤t≤8). Estimate the height for the moment wey the height biggest.
l-m-h2-b0d03-19.s.s1.prompt: Which one na good estimate of the maximum height?
l-m-h2-b0d03-19.s.s1.r.a: You read the value of t (8 seconds) as the height. You need to find h(4).
l-m-h2-b0d03-19.s.s1.r.c: For t=4 you only calculate 8t. You need to subtract t².
l-m-h2-b0d03-19.s.s1.r.d: This na the value wey you get if you put t=8 and calculate only 8t. h(8)=0.
l-m-h2-b0d03-19.s.s1.explain: From h'(t)=−2t+8=0 we get t=4. h(4)=−16+32=16m, so the maximum height na 16m.
l-m-h2-b0d03-19.s.s2.model.0: The height biggest for t=4, where h'(t)=−2t+8 na 0, so h(4)=16m or so.
l-m-h2-b0d03-19.s.s2.model.1: The ball highest for t=4, exactly midway between t=0 and t=8 where the height na 0, so h(4)=16m.

l-m-h2-b0d03-25.s.s1.explain: Di rate dey change from 1 to 13, so di total dey between 2 and 26L. If you estimate with di middle rate 4, e give about 8, and di real amount na 10L.
l-m-h2-b0d03-25.s.s2.model.0: Di rate dey between 1 and 13, so di total dey between 2 and 26. If middle rate of 4 continue for 2 minutes, e na about 8, so 8 to 12L reasonable.
l-m-h2-b0d03-25.s.s2.model.1: Multiply middle rate of 4, no be di first rate 1 or di last rate 13, by 2 minutes and you go get about 8, so we estimate about 8 to 12L.

l-m-h2-b0d04-13.goal: Estimate di cost wey go increase when you make 1 more after 100 to decide one size or range wey fit, and explain how you think am.
l-m-h2-b0d04-13.material: Di cost na C(x)=x²+10x (for units of 10,000 won). Now we dey make x=100 items. Use C'(100) to estimate di cost wey go increase when you make 1 more.

l-m-h2-b0d04-13.s.s1.r.d: You take all of C(100) as di increase.
l-m-h2-b0d04-13.s.s1.explain: C'(x)=2x+10, so C'(100)=210. Di cost wey go increase when you make 1 more na like 210 × 10,000 won, and di real value na 211 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h2-b0d04-13.s.s2.model.0: Di increase when you make 1 more near di instantaneous rate of change C'(100)=2·100+10=210, so e na like 210 × 10,000 won.
l-m-h2-b0d04-13.s.s2.model.1: Since x change by only 1, di change for cost na C'(100)×1≈210, wey almost same as di real calculation, 211.

l-m-h2-b0d05-16.title: Roughly how many ways dey to choose 5 out of 20?
l-m-h2-b0d05-16.goal: Estimate di number of ways to choose 5 from 20 different things, decide one correct size or range, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d05-16.material: You wan estimate, without calculator, di number of ways to choose 5 of 20 different objects. Di order wey you take choose no matter.
l-m-h2-b0d05-16.s.s1.r.a: Dem treat am like 20⁵, where dem allow repeats. If you choose without repeats, e go give less.
l-m-h2-b0d05-16.s.s1.r.b: Dis na di value of 20P5, wey dey count different orders separately. Since order no matter, you must divide by 5!.
l-m-h2-b0d05-16.s.s1.r.d: Dem look am as small as 20×5. Di number of ways big well well pass dat one.
l-m-h2-b0d05-16.s.s1.explain: From 20×19×18×17×16≈1,860,000 (186×10,000), di 5!=120 different orders count as one way, so if you divide by 120 e give about 15,000 (1×10,000 + 5×1,000).
l-m-h2-b0d05-16.s.s2.model.0: If you count different orders separately e give about 1,860,000 (186×10,000), but di 5!=120 ways to line up 5 items count as one, so if you divide by 120 e give about 15,000 (1×10,000 + 5×1,000).
l-m-h2-b0d05-16.s.s2.model.1: If you roughly take 20×19×18×17×16 as 1,860,000 (186×10,000) and divide by 120, e give about 15,000 (1×10,000 + 5×1,000), wey fit dis problem where order no matter.

l-m-h2-b0d05-17.topic: Meaning and use of probability (wetin probability mean and how to use am)
l-m-h2-b0d05-17.goal: Estimate di probability say di sum of three dice go be 10 or more, decide one correct size or range, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d05-17.material: Dem roll three fair dice at di same time. Di sum of di dots dey from 3 to 18, and di average sum na 10.5. Estimate di range of di probability say di sum go be 10 or more.
l-m-h2-b0d05-17.s.s1.prompt: Which one be di most correct range?
l-m-h2-b0d05-17.s.s1.r.a: Since di average na 10.5, 10 or more dey around half. Dis one too small.
l-m-h2-b0d05-17.s.s1.r.b: Even 11 or more don already be half, so 10 or more big pass dat one.
l-m-h2-b0d05-17.s.s1.r.d: Plenty values dey near di average, so 10 or more no be almost sure thing.
l-m-h2-b0d05-17.s.s1.explain: Di sum dey symmetric around 10.5, so 11 or more na half. If you add di cases where di sum na 10, e give 62.5%.
l-m-h2-b0d05-17.s.s2.model.0: Because di sum dey symmetric around 10.5, 11 or more na half, and dem add di cases where di sum na 10, so e small pass half small, 55~70%.
l-m-h2-b0d05-17.s.s2.model.1: Since di average na 10.5, we fit see 10 or more as small over half, so di range 55~70% fit.

l-m-h2-b0d05-18.title: How rare be height wey dey 2σ below di mean?
l-m-h2-b0d05-18.goal: Estimate di proportion of students wey short pass 160 cm, decide one correct size or range, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d05-18.material: Suppose di heights of students for one school follow one normal distribution with mean 170 cm and standard deviation 5 cm. Without standard normal table, estimate di proportion of students wey short pass 160 cm.
l-m-h2-b0d05-18.s.s1.r.a: Dis na value wey near mean-3σ. 160 na mean-2σ, so e big pass dat one.
l-m-h2-b0d05-18.s.s1.r.c: Dis na di proportion wey dey below mean-1σ. 160 dey farther out pass dat one.
l-m-h2-b0d05-18.s.s1.r.d: Dis na di sum of both sides wey pass 1σ from di mean. E no be only one tail.
l-m-h2-b0d05-18.s.s1.explain: 160 na mean-2σ. About 95% dey inside mean±2σ, so one tail na (100-95)÷2, about 2.5%.
l-m-h2-b0d05-18.s.s2.model.0: 160 na 170 minus 10, wey be 2 times σ, so na di lower one of di two 5% tails wey dey outside mean±2σ, about 2.5%.
l-m-h2-b0d05-18.s.s2.model.1: Since about 95% dey inside mean±2σ, below 160 na about half of di remaining 5%, so you fit estimate about 2~3%.

l-m-h2-b0d05-19.title: How to estimate di range of di population mean from one sample
l-m-h2-b0d05-19.goal: Estimate di range where di population mean fit dey, decide one correct size or range, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d05-19.material: Dem draw 100 people from one population wey get standard deviation 10, and di sample mean na 50. Take di coefficient for 95% confidence as about 2. Without calculator, estimate di range of di confidence interval for di population mean.
l-m-h2-b0d05-19.s.s1.prompt: Which one be di most correct confidence interval?
l-m-h2-b0d05-19.s.s1.r.a: Dem take ±2σ=±20. Di standard deviation of di sample mean na 10÷√100=1.
l-m-h2-b0d05-19.s.s1.r.b: Dem use di population standard deviation 10 as e be. Wit n=100 di interval narrow well well pass dat one.
l-m-h2-b0d05-19.s.s1.r.d: Dis one too narrow, like ±0.1. Di standard deviation of di sample mean na 1.
l-m-h2-b0d05-19.s.s1.explain: Di standard deviation of di sample mean na 10÷√100=1. 50±2×1 give about 48~52.
l-m-h2-b0d05-19.s.s2.model.0: Di standard deviation of di sample mean na 10÷10=1 and di coefficient na about 2, so e na 50±2, wey mean about 48~52.
l-m-h2-b0d05-19.s.s2.model.1: Wit sample of 100, e shrink to σ/√n=1, and if you take 2 times dat one for both sides, e give range between 48 and 52, wey fit.

l-m-h2-b0d06-14.goal: Estimate di probability of exactly 5 heads for 10 coin tosses so you fit decide suitable size or range, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h2-b0d06-14.material: Dem toss fair coin 10 times. 2¹⁰=1024 possible outcomes dey in all, di number of heads spread from 0 to 10, and di values near di middle, 5, dey come pass. Estimate di probability of exactly 5 heads.
l-m-h2-b0d06-14.s.s1.r.a: Di values spread over 11 possibilities, so di middle value big pass 1% well well.
l-m-h2-b0d06-14.s.s1.r.b: Di middle value na di one wey dey come pass, so e big pass 10%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-14.s.s1.r.d: 5 heads no be half of di probability. 4 and 6 heads dey come plenty too.
l-m-h2-b0d06-14.s.s1.explain: Di cases wey get 5 heads na 10C5=252, and di total na 1024. 252/1024≈0.25.
l-m-h2-b0d06-14.s.s2.model.0: If you estimate 10C5=252 as 250 and 1024 as 1000, e give about 1/4, so about 25%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-14.s.s2.model.1: Di number of heads spread over 11 values from 0 to 10, and di middle one big pass, so we fit estimate about 25%, wey big pass di even split of about 9%.

l-m-h2-b0d06-15.title: How to estimate di number of 4-letter uppercase codes
l-m-h2-b0d06-15.topic: Permutation with repetition (order matter, dem fit repeat)
l-m-h2-b0d06-15.goal: Estimate di number of 4-letter codes wey dem make from English uppercase letters so you fit decide suitable size or range, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h2-b0d06-15.material: Estimate di number of 4-letter codes wey dem make from di 26 English uppercase letters. Dem fit use di same letter more than once, and different order of letters make different code. No use calculator.
l-m-h2-b0d06-15.s.s1.r.a: I estimate 26 as 10. 26 big pass 10 well well, so di answer pass 10⁴.
l-m-h2-b0d06-15.s.s1.r.c: I add am, like 26×4=104. Each of di 4 places get 26 possibilities, so you must multiply.
l-m-h2-b0d06-15.s.s1.r.d: 26⁴ small pass 30⁴=81×10⁴ (810,000), so 1×10⁸ (100 million) too big.
l-m-h2-b0d06-15.s.s1.explain: Each place get 26 possibilities, so e be 26⁴. 26²=676 and 676²≈46×10⁴, so e na about 46×10⁴ (460,000).
l-m-h2-b0d06-15.s.s2.model.0: Each place get 26 possibilities, so e be 26×26×26×26. 26²≈700, so 700²≈49×10⁴ (490,000), and about 46×10⁴ (460,000) fit.
l-m-h2-b0d06-15.s.s2.model.1: E small pass 30⁴=81×10⁴ (810,000), wey estimate 26 as 30, and e big pass 20⁴=16×10⁴ (160,000), so about 46×10⁴ (460,000), wey dey between dem, fit.

l-m-h2-b0d06-16.goal: Estimate di score wey match di top 16% or so so you fit decide suitable size or range, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h2-b0d06-16.material: Di scores for one test follow normal distribution with mean of 70 points and standard deviation of 10 points. Use di fact say about 68% dey within 1 standard deviation of di mean to estimate di cutoff score for di top 16% or so.
l-m-h2-b0d06-16.s.s1.r.a: Na score wey dey below di mean, so e no fit dey inside di top 16%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-16.s.s1.r.b: Di mean na di cutoff for di top 50%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-16.s.s1.r.d: Dat one dey around di mean+3σ, wey be about di top 0.1%, e too high well well.
l-m-h2-b0d06-16.s.s1.explain: Within mean±σ na 68%, so outside for both sides na 32%, and one side na 16%. So mean+σ=80 points na di cutoff.
l-m-h2-b0d06-16.s.s2.model.0: Within mean±σ na about 68%, so one side outside na 16%, and e cutoff na mean+σ=70+10=80 points.
l-m-h2-b0d06-16.s.s2.model.1: Di top 16% na one standard deviation above di mean, so about 80 points fit. 70 points na di top 50%.

l-m-h2-b0d06-17.title: Di probability of 215 or more heads for 400 coin tosses
l-m-h2-b0d06-17.goal: Estimate di probability of 215 or more heads for 400 coin tosses to decide one correct size or range, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d06-17.material: Di number of heads X for 400 tosses of one fair coin dey roughly follow N(200, 10²). Without standard normal table, estimate di size of P(X≥215). 215 dey 1.5σ above di mean.
l-m-h2-b0d06-17.s.s1.r.a: 1.5σ above dey closer pass 2σ above (about 2.5%), so e big pass 1%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-17.s.s1.r.c: E dey farther pass 1σ above (about 16%), so e no fit pass 20%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-17.s.s1.r.d: E for be value wey near di mean to reach 40%. 1.5σ above rare well well pass dat one.
l-m-h2-b0d06-17.s.s1.explain: 1σ above na about 16% and 2σ above na about 2.5%, so 1.5σ above dey between dem, and if we wan be more exact e na about 6.7%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-17.s.s2.model.0: 1σ above na about 16% and 2σ above na about 2.5%, so we fit estimate say 1.5σ above dey between dem, 5 to 10%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-17.s.s2.model.1: 215 dey 1.5 times di standard deviation 10 above di mean 200, so e dey di tail, and one tail dey between 2.5% and 16%, so 5 to 10% fit.

l-m-h2-b0d06-18.title: Two dice sum reach 7: how many times out of 100?
l-m-h2-b0d06-18.goal: Estimate how many times di sum of two dice go be 7 to decide one correct size or range, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d06-18.material: Dem roll two dice and look di sum of di faces, and dem repeat dis trial 100 times. Di sum na 7 for 6 of di 36 possible cases. Estimate roughly how many times di sum 7 go show.
l-m-h2-b0d06-18.s.s1.prompt: Which one be di most correct number of times?
l-m-h2-b0d06-18.s.s1.r.a: Di probability na 1/6, so for 100 tries e go show plenty more times.
l-m-h2-b0d06-18.s.s1.r.b: Dem mistake di number 7 for di sum 7 as one count. You must use di probability 1/6.
l-m-h2-b0d06-18.s.s1.r.d: You no fit assume say half of di rolls go be 7. Di probability na 1/6.
l-m-h2-b0d06-18.s.s1.explain: Di probability say di sum na 7 na 6/36=1/6. 1/6 of 100 na about 17 times.
l-m-h2-b0d06-18.s.s2.model.0: Di probability say di sum na 7 na 6/36=1/6, so we estimate say e go show about 100×1/6≈17 times out of 100.
l-m-h2-b0d06-18.s.s2.model.1: E na 6 out of 36, wey be about once for every six tries, so for 100 tries e dey around 17 times.

l-m-h2-b0d01-02.title: Find di mistake for di solution of 9ˣ−3ˣ−6=0
l-m-h2-b0d01-02.goal: Follow di solution of 9ˣ−3ˣ−6=0 step by step, together with di chain of causes and results, then find di first place wey e go wrong and fix am.
l-m-h2-b0d01-02.material: Solution of 9ˣ−3ˣ−6=0. (1) Let t=3ˣ, so t²−t−6=0 (2) (t−3)(t+2)=0, so t=3 or t=−2 (3) If 3ˣ=3 then x=1, and if 3ˣ=−2 then x=−2 (4) So x=1 or x=−2
l-m-h2-b0d01-02.s.s1.o.a: (1) Di step wey dem write t²−t−6=0
l-m-h2-b0d01-02.s.s1.o.c: (3) Di step wey dem write x=−2 from 3ˣ=−2
l-m-h2-b0d01-02.s.s1.o.d: (4) Di step wey dem give both values as di answer

l-m-h2-b0d02-34.material: Proof of "n²+n na odd for every natural number n". (1) Assume k²+k na odd when n=k (2) (k+1)²+(k+1)=(k²+k)+2(k+1) (3) odd+even=odd, so e hold for n=k+1 too (4) E hold for every natural number n
l-m-h2-b0d02-34.s.s1.o.a: (1) Where e assume say di statement hold for n=k
l-m-h2-b0d02-34.s.s1.r.a: Na di assumption wey dem make for di induction step, so no wahala.
l-m-h2-b0d02-34.s.s1.o.b: (2) Where dem write di expression as (k²+k)+2(k+1)
l-m-h2-b0d02-34.s.s1.r.b: If you expand am, you go get di same expression, so e correct.
l-m-h2-b0d02-34.s.s1.o.d: (4) Where e conclude say e hold for all without to check n=1
l-m-h2-b0d02-34.s.s1.explain: Di base step n=1 miss. 1²+1=2 na even, and true true n²+n always be even.
l-m-h2-b0d02-34.s.s2.model.0: E get only di induction step and e no check di case n=1, so di proof no work. 1²+1=2 na even, so di statement false.
l-m-h2-b0d02-34.s.s2.model.1: If base step no dey, no starting point dey, so you no fit draw di conclusion for (4), and n²+n=n(n+1) always be even, so di statement itself wrong.

l-m-h2-b0d03-05.title: To cancel when di denominator na square: where e go wrong?
l-m-h2-b0d03-05.goal: Follow di steps of one solution wey find lim (x²−1)/(x−1)² (x→1) (di order of cause and result), find where e first go wrong, and fix am.
l-m-h2-b0d03-05.material: Solution: ① x²−1=(x−1)(x+1) ② If you cancel with di denominator (x−1)², only x+1 remain ③ As x→1, x+1→2 ④ Di limit na 2.
l-m-h2-b0d03-05.s.s1.prompt: Choose di first step wey wrong.
l-m-h2-b0d03-05.s.s1.o.b: ② To cancel and only x+1 remain

l-m-h2-b0d03-05.s.s1.r.d: Di conclusion wrong because of ②. Na no be where di first mistake dey.
l-m-h2-b0d03-05.s.s1.explain: (x−1)(x+1)/(x−1)²=(x+1)/(x−1). Since (x−1) remain for di denominator, di limit no dey.
l-m-h2-b0d03-05.s.s2.model.0: You fit cancel (x−1)² with (x−1) only one time, wey leave (x+1)/(x−1), so ② wrong.
l-m-h2-b0d03-05.s.s2.model.1: Because (x−1) remain for di denominator, di value dey grow or shrink without end as x→1, so no limit dey. ②, wey treat di canceling as finished, na di first error.

l-m-h2-b0d03-11.goal: Follow the steps of one solution wey find f'(2) for f(x)=x²+3x using the definition (the order of cause and result), find where e first go wrong, then fix am.
l-m-h2-b0d03-11.material: f(x)=x²+3x. Solution: ① f(2)=10 ② f(2+h)=4+h²+6+3h ③ (f(2+h)−f(2))/h=(h²+3h)/h=h+3 ④ As h→0, f'(2)=3.

l-m-h2-b0d03-11.s.s1.r.c: If we take the result of ②, this calculation correct. The place wey first go wrong na ②.
l-m-h2-b0d03-11.s.s1.r.d: The conclusion wrong, but the cause dey for earlier step.
l-m-h2-b0d03-11.s.s1.explain: (2+h)²=4+4h+h². Dem leave out the middle term 4h, so 3 come out instead of f'(2)=7.

l-m-h2-b0d03-26.material: Solution for di definite integral of |x| from −1 to 1: ① |x| na −x for x<0 and x for x≥0 ② So replace |x| with x and integrate everything at once ③ Di definite integral of x na [x²/2]=0 ④ So di value na 0.

l-m-h2-b0d03-26.s.s1.o.b: ② Replace |x| with x and integrate everything at once

l-m-h2-b0d05-21.goal: Follow the solution, or the chain of cause and effect, for the probability say one die show 3 when the sum na 7, step by step. Find the first place wey e go wrong and fix am.
l-m-h2-b0d05-21.material: Dis one na solution for the probability say one die show 3 when dem roll two dice and the sum na 7. Step 1: the cases wey sum na 7 be (1,6)(2,5)(3,4)(4,3)(5,2)(6,1), 6 ways. Step 2: inside dem, the cases wey get 3 be (3,4)(4,3), 2 ways. Step 3: the probability na 2/36=1/18.
l-m-h2-b0d05-21.s.s1.r.a: Dem list all the 6 cases wey sum na 7. Dis one correct.
l-m-h2-b0d05-21.s.s1.r.b: Dem find the 2 cases wey get 3 well. Dis one correct.
l-m-h2-b0d05-21.s.s1.r.d: To divide by all the 36 cases give the probability without the condition.
l-m-h2-b0d05-21.s.s1.explain: Because of the condition say the sum na 7, the total na 6 ways. So e be 2/6=1/3.
l-m-h2-b0d05-21.s.s2.model.0: For Step 3 dem divide by 36, but because of the condition say the sum na 7, the sample space shrink to 6 ways. So make una fix am to 2/6=1/3.
l-m-h2-b0d05-21.s.s2.model.1: Conditional probability na ratio inside the cases wey meet the condition, so the denominator na 6. 2/36 na value wey ignore the condition.

l-m-h2-b0d05-22.s.s1.r.c: The way wey dem take multiply correct. The value from the step before wrong.
l-m-h2-b0d05-22.s.s1.r.d: The probability na 15/4, wey pass 1, so something wrong.
l-m-h2-b0d05-22.s.s1.explain: Both 2 heads and 3 tails must happen, so una must multiply the probabilities, no add dem. (1/2)⁵=1/32 and the answer na 10/32=5/16.
l-m-h2-b0d05-22.s.s2.model.0: For Step 2, the probability say independent events all happen, una must multiply am, no add am. (1/2)²×(1/2)³=1/32, so the answer na 5/16.
l-m-h2-b0d05-22.s.s2.model.1: Probability no suppose pass 1, as 15/4 do, so una must multiply the probabilities instead of to add dem. One case na 1/32.

l-m-h2-b0d05-23.material: Dis one na solution for the coefficient of x² inside (2x+1)⁴. Step 1: the general term na 4Cr·2·xʳ·1^(4-r). Step 2: for x², r=2. Step 3: the coefficient na 4C2×2=12.

l-m-h2-b0d05-23.s.s2.model.0: For Step 1, dem write (2x)ʳ as 2xʳ, dem leave the r-th power of 2. Since 2²=4, make una fix the coefficient to 6×4=24.

l-m-h2-b0d05-24.goal: Follow the solution, or the chain of cause and effect, for how to find P(X≥120) inside normal distribution, step by step. Find the first place wey e go wrong and fix am.
l-m-h2-b0d05-24.material: Dis one na solution for P(X≥120) when X follow the normal distribution N(100, 10²). Step 1: standardize with Z=(X-100)/10. Step 2: P(X≥120)=P(Z≥2). Step 3: P(Z≥2)=P(0≤Z≤2)=0.4772.
l-m-h2-b0d05-24.s.s1.r.a: P(Z≥2) na the right tail, so e small pass 0.4772 well well.
l-m-h2-b0d05-24.s.s1.r.c: To subtract the mean 100 and divide by σ=10 na the correct way to standardize.
l-m-h2-b0d05-24.s.s1.r.d: Since (120-100)/10=2, to change am to P(Z≥2) correct.
l-m-h2-b0d05-24.s.s1.explain: P(0≤Z≤2) dey between 0 and 2. For 2 or more, subtract am from 0.5: 0.5-0.4772=0.0228.
l-m-h2-b0d05-24.s.s2.model.0: Step 3 find the probability between 0 and 2. Z≥2 na the right tail, so make una fix am to 0.5-0.4772=0.0228.
l-m-h2-b0d05-24.s.s2.model.1: Since P(Z≥0)=0.5, if you subtract 0.4772, the probability between 0 and 2, you go get the probability of 2 or more. So the answer na 0.0228.

l-m-h2-b0d01-05.s.s1.r.b: Dis one turn di logarithm to multiplication. Logarithm mean exponent.
l-m-h2-b0d01-05.s.s1.r.d: Dis one na equation wey dem swap di base and di exponent.
l-m-h2-b0d01-05.s.s1.explain: logₐb=x na di same as aˣ=b. From 8ˣ=4, 2³ˣ=2², so x=2/3.

l-m-h2-b0d01-05.s.s2.model.1: By di definition of a logarithm, logₐb=x ⇔ aˣ=b, so we fit write 8ˣ=4. Because 2³ˣ=2², 3x=2 and x=2/3.

l-m-h2-b0d01-11.goal: Express the graph of y=2ˣ wey shift 3 to the right for another form (equation, table, picture, words), then explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d01-11.material: We wan express the graph of y=2ˣ wey translate by 3 for the direction of the x-axis with multiplication or division.

l-m-h2-b0d01-11.s.s1.r.d: This na the graph wey shift 3 to the left. E be the same as to multiply by 8.
l-m-h2-b0d01-11.s.s1.explain: The equation wey shift 3 to the right na y=2^(x−3), and 2^(x−3)=2ˣ÷2³=2ˣ÷8.
l-m-h2-b0d01-11.s.s2.model.0: If you put x−3 for the place of x, e give y=2^(x−3), and since 2^(x−3)=2ˣ÷2³, we fit write y=2ˣ÷8.

l-m-h2-b0d01-16.title: To describe the sine of θ+π with unit circle
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.goal: Express sin(θ+π) as one point for the unit circle for another form (equation, table, picture, words), then explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.material: For the unit circle, make P(cosθ, sinθ) be the point where the terminal side of angle θ meet the circle. We wan express sin(θ+π) by relating the point Q where the terminal side of θ+π meet the circle to P.
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.s.s1.prompt: How dem take get Q by moving P?
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.s.s1.o.a: The point wey dem reflect across the x-axis
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.s.s1.r.a: Reflection across the x-axis represent the angle −θ.
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.s.s1.o.b: The point wey dem reflect across the origin
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.s.s1.o.c: The point wey dem reflect across the y-axis
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.s.s1.r.c: Reflection across the y-axis represent the angle π−θ.
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.s.s1.o.d: Dem move di point π go di right
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.s.s1.r.d: Dem turn am by π around di circle, dem no translate am.
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.s.s1.explain: If dem turn another π, e go reach di opposite point. Q=(−cosθ, −sinθ), so sin(θ+π)=−sinθ.
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.s.s2.model.0: If dem turn another half turn (π) from θ, e go reach di opposite point, so Q=(−cosθ, −sinθ) and sin(θ+π)=−sinθ.
l-m-h2-b0d01-16.s.s2.model.1: Reflection across di origin dey change di signs of both di x and y coordinates, so di y coordinate sinθ go become −sinθ.

l-m-h2-b0d01-27.title: Which kain sequence you go get if you take log of a geometric sequence?
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.goal: Show di sequence wey you make by taking di logarithm of each term of a geometric sequence for another way (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.material: Look di sequence log₂3, log₂6, log₂12, log₂24, … wey you get by taking log₂ of each term of di geometric sequence 3, 6, 12, 24, ….
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.s.s1.prompt: Which kain sequence be this one?
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.s.s1.o.a: E no be arithmetic sequence and e no be geometric sequence
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.s.s1.r.a: Di difference na always di constant 1, so e be arithmetic sequence.
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.s.s1.o.b: A geometric sequence wey get common ratio 2
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.s.s1.r.b: Di difference between neighboring terms dey constant, but di ratio no dey constant.
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.s.s1.o.c: An arithmetic sequence wey get common difference 2
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.s.s1.r.c: Di difference between neighboring terms na log₂2=1, e no be 2.
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.s.s1.o.d: An arithmetic sequence wey get common difference 1
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.s.s1.explain: Since log₂aₙ=log₂3+(n−1)·log₂2, e be arithmetic sequence wey dey increase by 1 for each term.
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.s.s2.model.0: Since log₂aₙ=log₂3+(n−1)·log₂2, e be arithmetic sequence wey get common difference 1, wey dey increase by 1 for each term.
l-m-h2-b0d01-27.s.s2.model.1: Because di ratio of neighboring terms na 2, when you take di logarithm, di difference go always be di constant 1, like log₂6−log₂3=log₂2=1.

l-m-h2-b0d01-31.title: How to Rewrite di Starting Point of a Sigma
l-m-h2-b0d01-31.goal: Change di sum wey dem write with sigma to another way to show am (expression, table, picture, or words), and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d01-31.material: Di sum Σ_{k=3}^{7} (k−2) mean say you add (k−2) from k=3 reach 7. We wan find another sigma expression wey get di same value.

l-m-h2-b0d01-31.s.s1.r.d: E add from −1 reach 3, so di value different.

l-m-h2-b0d01-36.material: Dem dey compare mathematical induction to dominoes. We wan talk ‘e hold for n=1’ and ‘if e hold for n=k, e hold for n=k+1 too’ again with domino words.
l-m-h2-b0d01-36.s.s1.prompt: Which statement match ‘if e hold for n=k, e hold for n=k+1 too’?
l-m-h2-b0d01-36.s.s1.r.a: Na di first step, to check di case n=1.
l-m-h2-b0d01-36.s.s1.o.b: All di dominoes don already fall
l-m-h2-b0d01-36.s.s1.r.b: This one match di conclusion wey we wan prove.
l-m-h2-b0d01-36.s.s1.o.c: Di k-th domino big pass di (k+1)-th one

l-m-h2-b0d01-36.s.s2.model.1: To knock down only di first domino no reach, so di link say when any domino fall, di one wey follow am go fall too na di induction step.

l-m-h2-b0d02-19.title: How to Describe di cos Graph as Shift of di sin Graph
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.goal: Change di description of y=cosx as translation of y=sinx to another way to show am (an expression, a table, a picture, or words), and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.material: We wan show di graph of y=cos x as translation of di graph of y=sin x.
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.s.s1.o.a: y=sin x wey dem shift go left by π/2
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.s.s1.o.b: y=sin x wey dem shift go up by π/2
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.s.s1.r.b: To shift go up only dey add π/2 to di y-values, wey different from cos x.
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.s.s1.o.c: y=sin x wey dem shift go right by π
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.s.s1.r.c: sin(x−π)=−sin x, so e no be cos x.
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.s.s1.o.d: y=sin x wey dem shift go right by π/2
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.s.s1.r.d: sin(x−π/2)=−cos x, so e don turn upside down.
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.s.s1.explain: cos x=sin(x+π/2). If you shift di sin graph go left by π/2, you go get di cos graph.
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.s.s2.model.0: Since cos x=sin(x+π/2), na y=sin x wey dem change x to x+π/2, dat mean di graph wey dem shift go left by π/2.
l-m-h2-b0d02-19.s.s2.model.1: sin x reach 1 for x=π/2 and cos x reach 1 for x=0, so if you shift di sin graph go left by π/2, e go cover di cos graph.

l-m-h2-b0d02-28.title: To describe di common difference of an arithmetic sequence as di slope of a line
l-m-h2-b0d02-28.goal: Rewrite di common difference of an arithmetic sequence for di coordinate plane for another form (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d02-28.material: If you plot di points (n, aₙ) of di arithmetic sequence aₙ=2n+1 for di coordinate plane, you go get (1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 7), …, and dis points dey lie for one line.
l-m-h2-b0d02-28.s.s1.prompt: Wetin for di line equal di common difference of dis sequence?
l-m-h2-b0d02-28.s.s1.r.a: Di y-intercept 1 na di value for n=0. Di common difference na 2.
l-m-h2-b0d02-28.s.s1.r.c: Di x-intercept na di value of n when aₙ=0. E differ from di common difference.
l-m-h2-b0d02-28.s.s1.o.d: Di distance between di origin and di line
l-m-h2-b0d02-28.s.s1.r.d: Dat distance no get anything to do with di common difference.
l-m-h2-b0d02-28.s.s1.explain: When n increase by 1, aₙ increase by 2. So di slope na 2, equal to di common difference 2.
l-m-h2-b0d02-28.s.s2.model.0: Because aₙ dey increase by 2 each time n increase by 1, di slope na 2, wey equal di common difference 2.
l-m-h2-b0d02-28.s.s2.model.1: Di slope of di line through di points (1, 3) and (2, 5) na (5−3)/(2−1)=2, so we fit talk say e equal di common difference.

l-m-h2-b0d03-06.title: How to rewrite "continuous for x=2" as equation
l-m-h2-b0d03-06.goal: Rewrite di statement "e continuous for x=2" for another form (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d03-06.material: We wan rewrite di statement say function f continuous for x=2 as equation wey use di limit and di function value.
l-m-h2-b0d03-06.s.s1.r.b: Say di function value na 0 no get anything to do with continuity.
l-m-h2-b0d03-06.s.s1.r.c: Di limit no need to be 0. E must equal f(2).
l-m-h2-b0d03-06.s.s1.r.d: This one mean constant function, wey too narrow.
l-m-h2-b0d03-06.s.s1.explain: Continuous mean say di limit dey and im value equal di function value f(2).
l-m-h2-b0d03-06.s.s2.model.0: As x dey near 2, f(x) dey near f(2), so e mean di same thing as di equation wey talk say di limit and di function value equal.
l-m-h2-b0d03-06.s.s2.model.1: To dey connected with no break mean say di limit dey and im value na f(2), so you fit write am as lim f(x)=f(2).

l-m-h2-b0d03-16.title: Sign change of the derivative as graph shape
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.goal: Rewrite the statement "the sign of f' change from + to − for x=2" for another form (expression, table, diagram, or words) then explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.material: For the left of x=2, f'(x)>0, and for the right, f'(x)<0, and f continuous for x=2. Talk this again in terms of the shape of the graph of f.
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.s.s1.prompt: Choose the statement wey mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.s.s1.o.a: For x=2 e go down, then go up, and reach bottom
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.s.s1.r.a: To go from + to − mean increasing and then decreasing, so e be peak (local maximum).
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.s.s1.o.b: For x=2 e keep going up
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.s.s1.r.b: For the right, f'<0, so e go down.
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.s.s1.o.c: For x=2 e go up, then go down, and reach peak
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.s.s1.r.d: Since f continuous, e no break.
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.s.s1.explain: If f'>0, f dey increase, and if f'<0, f dey decrease. For x=2, where e change from increasing to decreasing, local maximum dey.
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.s.s2.model.0: For the left f'>0 so the graph dey go up, and for the right f'<0 so e dey go down, so the shape get local maximum for x=2.
l-m-h2-b0d03-16.s.s2.model.1: Because e change from increasing to decreasing, peak dey for x=2, and this mean the same as the sign of the derivative wey change from + to −.

l-m-h2-b0d03-27.title: To turn a definite integral into an area formula
l-m-h2-b0d03-27.goal: Rewrite di definite integral of di velocity v(t)=2t from 0 to 4 seconds for another form (expression, table, diagram, or words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d03-27.material: Di velocity of one point na v(t)=2t (m/s). Look di distance ∫2t dt wey e travel from 0 seconds to 4 seconds as one shape under di graph, and turn am to area formula.
l-m-h2-b0d03-27.s.s1.prompt: Choose di expression wey give di same value.
l-m-h2-b0d03-27.s.s1.r.a: Na di area of a rectangle. Under di graph one triangle dey, so na half.
l-m-h2-b0d03-27.s.s1.r.b: You take di height to be 2. For t=4, v=8.
l-m-h2-b0d03-27.s.s1.r.c: You take di base to be 8. Di length of di interval na 4.
l-m-h2-b0d03-27.s.s1.explain: Under y=2t one triangle dey wey get base 4 and height v(4)=8. Im area, 16, equal di value of di definite integral.
l-m-h2-b0d03-27.s.s2.model.0: Between di graph of v=2t and di t-axis one right triangle dey wey get base 4 and height 8, so im area (1/2)×4×8=16 equal di definite integral.
l-m-h2-b0d03-27.s.s2.model.1: Di velocity na 8 for t=4 and e dey increase steadily from 0 to 4, so di shape na triangle, and dem fit write di definite integral as (1/2)×4×8.

l-m-h2-b0d03-28.title: To talk di meaning of an indefinite integral with differentiation
l-m-h2-b0d03-28.goal: Rewrite di indefinite integral ∫(3x²+2x)dx for another form (expression, table, diagram, or words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d03-28.material: ∫(3x²+2x)dx = x³+x²+C. Use differentiation to talk for another way wetin an indefinite integral mean.
l-m-h2-b0d03-28.s.s1.o.a: All functions wey give 3x²+2x when dem differentiate am
l-m-h2-b0d03-28.s.s1.r.b: Di direction don reverse. Na di function before dem differentiate, no be di result of differentiating.
l-m-h2-b0d03-28.s.s1.o.c: One area under di graph of 3x²+2x
l-m-h2-b0d03-28.s.s1.r.c: E no be di value of one area, but na collection of functions.
l-m-h2-b0d03-28.s.s1.r.d: Even if C differ, to differentiate go give di same result, so x³+x²+5 count too.
l-m-h2-b0d03-28.s.s1.explain: Whatever C be, to differentiate x³+x²+C give 3x²+2x. Di indefinite integral mean all such functions.
l-m-h2-b0d03-28.s.s2.model.0: To differentiate x³+x²+C make C disappear and give 3x²+2x, so di indefinite integral na all di functions wey give 3x²+2x when dem differentiate am.
l-m-h2-b0d03-28.s.s2.model.1: Even if di constant C differ, di result of differentiating na di same, so e no mean one function but all di functions wey give 3x²+2x when dem differentiate am.

l-m-h2-b0d04-06.title: How to rewrite |x−3|/(x−3) by interval
l-m-h2-b0d04-06.goal: Rewrite di expression |x−3|/(x−3) for another form (expression, table, diagram, or words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d04-06.material: We wan write f(x)=|x−3|/(x−3) (x≠3) by interval without di absolute value. E dey help when you wan draw di graph or check di limits from di left and right.
l-m-h2-b0d04-06.s.s1.prompt: Pick di one wey show di same function.
l-m-h2-b0d04-06.s.s1.r.a: Di signs don turn back to front. If you put x=4 e give 1.
l-m-h2-b0d04-06.s.s1.r.d: Di numerator and di denominator get di same size, so di value na ±1.
l-m-h2-b0d04-06.s.s1.explain: If x>3, |x−3|=x−3 so di quotient na 1, and if x<3, |x−3|=−(x−3) so di quotient na −1.
l-m-h2-b0d04-06.s.s2.model.0: If x>3, |x−3|=x−3 so di quotient na 1, and if x<3, |x−3|=−(x−3) so e na −1.
l-m-h2-b0d04-06.s.s2.model.1: If you put x=4 e give 1/1=1, and if you put x=2 e give 1/(−1)=−1, so by interval e na 1 and −1.

l-m-h2-b0d04-16.title: How to write derivative f'(3) for another form
l-m-h2-b0d04-16.goal: Write derivative f'(3) for another form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d04-16.material: f'(3) na di limit of (f(3+h)−f(3))/h as h→0. Make x=3+h and use variable x write am as expression wey get di same meaning.
l-m-h2-b0d04-16.s.s1.r.a: If f continuous, e go become 0, so e no be rate of change.
l-m-h2-b0d04-16.s.s1.r.b: Di part wey dey subtract f(3) and di part wey dey divide by x−3 no dey.
l-m-h2-b0d04-16.s.s1.r.c: Na di average rate of change from x=0 reach 3.
l-m-h2-b0d04-16.s.s1.explain: If x=3+h, then h=x−3, and h→0 mean say x→3. So di limit of (f(x)−f(3))/(x−3) na f'(3).
l-m-h2-b0d04-16.s.s2.model.0: When you set x=3+h, h go equal x−3 and h→0 go become x→3, so di two expressions na di same limit wey get different names.
l-m-h2-b0d04-16.s.s2.model.1: Di numerator na f(3+h)−f(3)=f(x)−f(3) and di denominator na h=x−3, so di new expression get di same value as di original one.

l-m-h2-b0d04-17.title: How to show tangent information with f and f'
l-m-h2-b0d04-17.goal: Write di statement "di slope of di tangent for point (2, 5) na 3" for another form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d04-17.material: Di slope of di tangent line to di curve y=f(x) for point (2, 5) na 3. We wan write dis statement as expression wey use f and f'.
l-m-h2-b0d04-17.s.s1.r.b: Dem swap di x- and y-coordinates. Di point na x=2, y=5.
l-m-h2-b0d04-17.s.s1.r.c: Dem swap di function value and di slope.
l-m-h2-b0d04-17.s.s1.r.d: Dem use di y-coordinate 5 as di derivative value instead of di slope.
l-m-h2-b0d04-17.s.s1.explain: Because di curve pass through (2, 5), f(2)=5, and di slope of di tangent for dat point na f'(2)=3.
l-m-h2-b0d04-17.s.s2.model.0: Because point (2, 5) dey for di curve, f(2)=5, and di slope of di tangent na di derivative value, so f'(2)=3.
l-m-h2-b0d04-17.s.s2.model.1: Di function value for x-coordinate 2 na 5, so f(2)=5, and di slope for dat point na 3, so we write f'(2)=3.

l-m-h2-b0d04-26.title: How to write di change for position as definite integral
l-m-h2-b0d04-26.goal: Write di change for position from t=1 to t=5 for another form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d04-26.material: For one point wey dey move along line, make s(t) be im position and v(t) im velocity for time t. We wan write di amount wey di position change from t=1 to t=5, s(5)−s(1), as definite integral.
l-m-h2-b0d04-26.s.s1.r.a: Dis one na di change for velocity. E no be di change for position.
l-m-h2-b0d04-26.s.s1.o.b: Di definite integral of v(t) from 1 to 5
l-m-h2-b0d04-26.s.s1.o.c: Di definite integral of s(t) from 1 to 5
l-m-h2-b0d04-26.s.s1.r.c: If you integrate position e go give form like position times time.
l-m-h2-b0d04-26.s.s1.r.d: Dis one na di average of di two positions. E no be di change.
l-m-h2-b0d04-26.s.s1.explain: Because s'(t)=v(t), to integrate v from 1 to 5 give s(5)−s(1). To integrate velocity give di change for position.
l-m-h2-b0d04-26.s.s2.model.0: Velocity v na di derivative of position s, so to integrate v from 1 to 5 give s(5)−s(1), wey equal di change for position.
l-m-h2-b0d04-26.s.s2.model.1: If you multiply di instantaneous velocity by short time and add everything together, e give di distance wey e move, so di definite integral of v from 1 to 5 na s(5)−s(1).

l-m-h2-b0d05-25.goal: Talk the number of non-negative integer solutions of x+y+z=5 again for another form (equation, table, picture, or words), and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.material: You wan count the non-negative integer triples (x, y, z) wey satisfy the equation x+y+z=5. If you turn dis one to everyday situation, think about which problem mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.s.s1.prompt: Choose the problem wey mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.s.s1.o.a: To share 5 different things among 3 people
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.s.s1.r.a: Na 3⁵ problem of how to decide who go get each item, so e different from the solutions wey sum na 5.
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.s.s1.o.b: To arrange 5 of 3 things for order
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.s.s1.r.b: You no fit choose 5 from 3. Na different situation from the number of solutions.
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.s.s1.o.c: To choose 3 from 5 kinds, repeats allowed
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.s.s1.r.c: Dem swap the number of kinds and the number wey dem choose. 3H5 and 5H3 different.
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.s.s1.o.d: To choose 5 from 3 kinds, repeats allowed
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.s.s1.explain: If x, y, z na the numbers of the three kinds, na the number of ways wey sum na 5. Dis one equal the combination with repetition 3H5=7C2=21.
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.s.s2.model.0: If x, y, z na the numbers wey dem choose for each kind, the sum na 5, so e mean the same thing as to choose 5 from 3 kinds with repeats allowed.
l-m-h2-b0d05-25.s.s2.model.1: To decide how many to choose for each kind be the same thing as to decide the solution (x, y, z), so e equal 3H5, wey be 21 ways.

l-m-h2-b0d05-26.s.s2.model.1: Every time wey you choose, the 5 wey remain don set, so the number of cases the same, and 8C3 and 8C5 get the same value, 56.

l-m-h2-b0d05-27.title: Write 'girl among students wey wear glasses' with symbols
l-m-h2-b0d05-27.goal: Talk 'the probability of to be girl among students wey wear glasses' again for another form (equation, table, picture, or words), and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d05-27.material: Among 100 students, 40 na girls and 38 wear glasses, and 20 girls wear glasses. When dem choose one student, talk 'the probability say the student na girl, among students wey wear glasses' again with symbols.
l-m-h2-b0d05-27.s.s1.prompt: Choose the symbol wey mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d05-27.s.s1.r.a: Dis one na the probability to wear glasses among girls. The condition and the result swap.
l-m-h2-b0d05-27.s.s1.r.c: Dis one na the probability to be girl or to wear glasses, so the meaning different.
l-m-h2-b0d05-27.s.s1.r.d: Dis one na the probability to be girl wey wear glasses among everybody. No condition dey.
l-m-h2-b0d05-27.s.s1.explain: 'Among students wey wear glasses' na the condition. So P(girl|glasses)=20/38, wey different from P(glasses|girl)=20/40.
l-m-h2-b0d05-27.s.s2.model.0: 'Among students wey wear glasses' na the condition and wetin we want na girl, so P(girl|glasses)=20/38. The condition dey come after |.
l-m-h2-b0d05-27.s.s2.model.1: For conditional probability, the event wey don happen dey after |, so P(girl|glasses), with glasses last, mean the same thing.

l-m-h2-b0d05-28.title: To change the interval of N(80, 4²) to standard normal
l-m-h2-b0d05-28.goal: Talk the interval probability P(76≤X≤88) of normal distribution again for another form (equation, table, picture, or words), and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d05-28.material: When X follow the normal distribution N(80, 4²), you wan change P(76≤X≤88) to Z, wey follow the standard normal distribution, so you fit use the standard normal table.
l-m-h2-b0d05-28.s.s1.prompt: Which one show the same probability?
l-m-h2-b0d05-28.s.s1.r.a: Dem subtract only the mean, dem no divide by σ=4.
l-m-h2-b0d05-28.s.s1.r.b: Dem swap the signs of the two endpoints. 76 dey below the mean.
l-m-h2-b0d05-28.s.s1.r.c: Dem divide only one endpoint by σ, and for the other one dem only subtract the mean.
l-m-h2-b0d05-28.s.s1.explain: Since Z=(X-80)/4, 76 become -1 and 88 become 2. To standardize mean to subtract the mean and divide by σ.
l-m-h2-b0d05-28.s.s2.model.0: If you subtract the mean 80 from each endpoint and divide by σ=4, 76 turn to -1 and 88 turn to 2, so e be the same probability as P(-1≤Z≤2).
l-m-h2-b0d05-28.s.s2.model.1: To standardize na (X-80)/4, so both endpoints must enter the same formula. Dat one give -1 and 2.

l-m-h2-b0d05-29.s.s2.model.1: If exactly 2 defective, the other 18 must be normal, so (0.9)¹⁸ go enter, and the position choice 20C2 go enter front.

l-m-h2-b0d06-23.goal: Change di value of 9C3+9C4 to another form (expression, table, picture, or words), and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d06-23.material: We wan rewrite 9C3+9C4 as one single combination without calculating. Think about how to choose 4 out of 10 different items by splitting am into cases by 'whether dem choose one particular item'.
l-m-h2-b0d06-23.s.s1.r.c: Dem add 9 and 9 and take am as 18. For combinations, you no dey add di upper numbers.
l-m-h2-b0d06-23.s.s1.r.d: 9C7=36, so e different from di sum 210.
l-m-h2-b0d06-23.s.s1.explain: Wen you dey choose 4 out of 10, if dem choose one particular one, dem choose 3 from di other 9 (9C3); if dem no choose am, dem choose 4 from 9 (9C4). Di sum na 10C4.
l-m-h2-b0d06-23.s.s2.model.0: Wen you dey choose 4 out of 10, if you add di case wey dem choose one particular one, 9C3, and di case wey dem no choose am, 9C4, e give all di cases, so e equal 10C4.
l-m-h2-b0d06-23.s.s2.model.1: If you add 9C3=84 and 9C4=126 e give 210, and 10C4 na 210 too, so di two expressions na di same number.

l-m-h2-b0d06-24.title: Two white balls one after di other, wey dem write another way
l-m-h2-b0d06-24.goal: Change di probability of drawing two white balls one after di other to another form (expression, table, picture, or words), and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d06-24.material: From one bag wey get 3 white balls and 5 black balls, dem draw balls without putting dem back, and we wan rewrite di probability 3/8×2/7 of getting white two times in a row as another expression. We fit think am as drawing 2 balls at once too.
l-m-h2-b0d06-24.s.s1.prompt: Which expression show di same probability?
l-m-h2-b0d06-24.s.s1.r.a: Dis na di expression for di case wey dem put di drawn ball back. Di second probability no be 2/7.
l-m-h2-b0d06-24.s.s1.r.b: Dem only change di denominator to permutation, so e mix up with one value wey dey separate order.
l-m-h2-b0d06-24.s.s1.r.c: Events wey happen one after di other, dem must multiply dem, no add dem.
l-m-h2-b0d06-24.s.s1.explain: 3C2/8C2=3/28 and 3/8×2/7=6/56=3/28, so dem equal. Even if dem draw 2 balls without caring about order, di probability still be di same.
l-m-h2-b0d06-24.s.s2.model.0: Di probability say both balls na white wen dem draw 2 at once na 3C2/8C2=3/28, wey equal 3/8×2/7=3/28, so dem mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d06-24.s.s2.model.1: Di numerator na di number of ways to choose 2 out of di 3 white balls, and di denominator na di number of ways to choose 2 out of all 8 balls, so dem fit rewrite am as 3C2/8C2.

l-m-h2-b0d06-25.title: Di distribution of di number of 6s on one die
l-m-h2-b0d06-25.goal: Change di distribution of di number of 6s for 20 rolls of one die to another form (expression, table, picture, or words), and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d06-25.material: Make X be di number of times wey 6 show wen dem roll one die 20 times. Di probability of 6 na di same for every roll, and di rolls independent of each other. Write di distribution wey X follow with binomial distribution notation.
l-m-h2-b0d06-25.s.s1.r.a: Dem swap di number of trials 20 and di success probability 1/6.
l-m-h2-b0d06-25.s.s1.r.c: Dem take di probability wrongly as 1/2 because two cases dey, 'a 6 show' and 'e no show'.
l-m-h2-b0d06-25.s.s1.r.d: Di success probability must dey between 0 and 1. 6 na di value wey dey on di die.
l-m-h2-b0d06-25.s.s1.explain: For 20 independent trials, di probability of success (to roll 6) na 1/6, so X follow B(20, 1/6).
l-m-h2-b0d06-25.s.s2.model.0: Di number of rolls na 20, di probability of 6 na di same 1/6 each time, and di rolls independent, so X follow B(20, 1/6).
l-m-h2-b0d06-25.s.s2.model.1: If dem define success as to roll 6, di success probability na 1/6 because e be one of di 6 faces, so dem write am as binomial distribution with n=20, p=1/6.

l-m-h2-b0d06-26.title: Di symmetry of di normal distribution, wey dem write another way
l-m-h2-b0d06-26.goal: Change one probability wey equal P(X≥54) for one normal distribution to another form (expression, table, picture, or words), and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d06-26.material: Wen X follow di normal distribution N(50, 4²), we wan rewrite P(X≥54) as another expression for di same probability. Di curve of di normal distribution dey symmetric for left and right around di mean 50.
l-m-h2-b0d06-26.s.s1.r.a: Na di probability wey add with P(X≥54) to make 1, so dem no equal.
l-m-h2-b0d06-26.s.s1.r.b: Na di middle interval around di mean, so e different from one tail probability.
l-m-h2-b0d06-26.s.s1.r.d: 46 or more include pass half, so e different.
l-m-h2-b0d06-26.s.s1.explain: 54 dey 4 above di mean, and its symmetric partner 46 dey 4 below. Di areas of di tails equal, so P(X≥54)=P(X≤46).
l-m-h2-b0d06-26.s.s2.model.0: 54, wey dey 4 to di right of di mean 50, and 46, wey dey 4 to di left, symmetric, so di probabilities of di right tail and di left tail equal.
l-m-h2-b0d06-26.s.s2.model.1: If you standardize, e give P(Z≥1), and P(X≤46) become P(Z≤-1), so by symmetry di two values equal.

l-m-h2-b0d06-27.title: To rewrite 'at least one' as one expression
l-m-h2-b0d06-27.goal: Change 'at least one of A or B happen' to another form (expression, table, picture, or words), and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-h2-b0d06-27.material: For two events A and B, we wan turn di statement 'at least one of A and B happen' to one probability expression. If we think from di side wey e no happen, we fit write am more simple.
l-m-h2-b0d06-27.s.s1.r.a: Dem add di overlapping part two times, so e fit become bigger than P(A∪B).

l-m-h2-b0d02-29.title: 1, −2, 4, −8, … na geometric sequence?
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.goal: Compare two methods or claims about whether a sequence wey get negative common ratio na geometric sequence, choose di one wey better pass, and explain di reasons.
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.material: Pipo get different opinions about whether di sequence 1, −2, 4, −8, 16, … na geometric sequence. Make we compare di opinions.
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.s.s1.prompt: Which opinion get di most correct reasoning?
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.s.s1.o.a: No: because di difference of neighboring terms no dey constant
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.s.s1.r.a: Whether di difference dey constant na di criterion for arithmetic sequence.
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.s.s1.o.b: No: because di signs dey alternate
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.s.s1.r.b: E still be geometric sequence even if di common ratio na negative.
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.s.s1.o.c: Yes, e be geometric: di ratio of neighboring terms na always −2
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.s.s1.o.d: No: because di common ratio no fit be negative
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.s.s1.r.d: Di common ratio fit be any real number apart from 0. Negative values fit happen too.
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.s.s1.explain: −2/1, 4/(−2), and −8/4 all na −2. If di ratio of neighboring terms dey constant, e be geometric sequence.
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.s.s2.model.0: −2÷1, 4÷(−2), and −8÷4 all na −2, so di ratio of neighboring terms dey constant, and e be geometric sequence wey get common ratio −2.
l-m-h2-b0d02-29.s.s2.model.1: Di criterion for geometric sequence na say di ratio dey constant, so even if di signs dey alternate, e be geometric if di ratio na di same −2.

l-m-h2-b0d03-07.title: To put big number versus to rationalize: which one sure pass?
l-m-h2-b0d03-07.goal: Compare two methods or claims for di limit of √(x²+4x)−x for infinity, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reasons.
l-m-h2-b0d03-07.material: A put x=100 and get √10400−100≈1.98 and talk say di limit na about 2. B rationalize di numerator to 4x/(√(x²+4x)+x), then find di limit and talk say e na 2.
l-m-h2-b0d03-07.s.s1.prompt: Which one show more sure say di limit na 2?
l-m-h2-b0d03-07.s.s1.o.a: A: To put x=100 sure pass
l-m-h2-b0d03-07.s.s1.r.a: One single value no fit settle limit.
l-m-h2-b0d03-07.s.s1.o.b: B: To change di expression by rationalizing sure pass
l-m-h2-b0d03-07.s.s1.r.c: To put number na estimate, but to rationalize settle am with expression.
l-m-h2-b0d03-07.s.s1.o.d: None of dem fit find di limit
l-m-h2-b0d03-07.s.s1.explain: To put number na estimate for one point. To rationalize give 4/(√(1+4/x)+1), wey show with expression say di limit na 2 as x→∞.
l-m-h2-b0d03-07.s.s2.model.0: To put only x=100 tell you only that one value, so e no fit settle di limit, but to rationalize show with expression say e na 2, so B sure pass.
l-m-h2-b0d03-07.s.s2.model.1: To rationalize give 4/(√(1+4/x)+1), wey show why e go 4/2=2 as x dey grow, so B fit pass.

l-m-h2-b0d03-17.title: When f'(a)=0, the tangent line: who correct?
l-m-h2-b0d03-17.goal: Compare two methods or claims about the tangent line of f(x)=x²−4x+7 for x=2, choose the better one, then explain your evidence.
l-m-h2-b0d03-17.material: For f(x)=x²−4x+7, f'(2)=0. A talk say "the tangent line na the x-axis (y=0)", and B talk say "the tangent line na the line y=3, wey parallel to the x-axis".
l-m-h2-b0d03-17.s.s1.prompt: Compare the two claims and choose the correct one.
l-m-h2-b0d03-17.s.s1.r.a: Only the slope na 0, and f(2)=3, so e no be y=0.
l-m-h2-b0d03-17.s.s1.r.c: Only one tangent line dey, so y=0 and y=3 no fit both correct.
l-m-h2-b0d03-17.s.s1.r.d: B correct because na line wey get slope 0 wey pass through the point (2,3).
l-m-h2-b0d03-17.s.s1.explain: The tangent line na the line y=3, with slope 0, wey pass through the point (2, f(2))=(2, 3).
l-m-h2-b0d03-17.s.s2.model.0: The slope na 0, so the line horizontal, and the point of tangency na (2,3), so the tangent line na y=3 and B correct.
l-m-h2-b0d03-17.s.s2.model.1: f'(2)=0 only tell us the slope, and f(2)=3 decide the height wey e pass through, so the x-axis y=0 no be the tangent line.

l-m-h2-b0d03-29.title: Area between two curves: di order of subtraction matter?
l-m-h2-b0d03-29.goal: Compare two methods or claims about di area between y=x² and y=3x, choose di better one, and explain your evidence.
l-m-h2-b0d03-29.material: y=x² and y=3x meet for x=0 and 3. A talk say di definite integral of (x²−3x) na −9/2, so di area na −9/2, and B talk say di definite integral of (3x−x²) na 9/2, so di area na 9/2.
l-m-h2-b0d03-29.s.s1.prompt: Choose di correct statement about di area.
l-m-h2-b0d03-29.s.s1.o.b: A: Subtract di upper from di lower
l-m-h2-b0d03-29.s.s1.r.b: Di order of upper and lower don reverse, so di sign come out negative.
l-m-h2-b0d03-29.s.s1.o.c: B: Subtract di lower expression from di upper expression
l-m-h2-b0d03-29.s.s1.o.d: Both talk say di area na 9/2
l-m-h2-b0d03-29.s.s1.r.d: A's value na −9/2, so di sign differ.
l-m-h2-b0d03-29.s.s1.explain: For 0≤x≤3, 3x≥x². Di area na di integral of (upper)−(lower), wey be 9/2. If you swap di order, only di sign go change.
l-m-h2-b0d03-29.s.s2.model.0: For di interval y=3x dey on top, so we must integrate (3x−x²), and di area positive, so B correct.
l-m-h2-b0d03-29.s.s2.model.1: Area no fit be negative, and we must subtract di lower x² from di upper 3x to get 0 or more, so B, with 9/2, correct.

l-m-h2-b0d04-07.title: Maximum of a continuous function: closed interval matter?
l-m-h2-b0d04-07.goal: Compare two methods or claims about di maximum value of f(x)=1/x for di interval (0,1], pick di better one, and explain your evidence.
l-m-h2-b0d04-07.material: f(x)=1/x continuous for di interval (0,1]. A talk say "since e be continuous function, e get maximum value for dis interval", and B talk say "since di interval no closed, we no fit promise say maximum value dey".
l-m-h2-b0d04-07.s.s1.o.a: A: If e continuous, maximum value dey
l-m-h2-b0d04-07.s.s1.r.a: Di near x reach 0, di bigger f dey go, so maximum value no dey.
l-m-h2-b0d04-07.s.s1.r.b: A wrong. f dey grow without end, so maximum value no dey.
l-m-h2-b0d04-07.s.s1.o.c: B: Di closed interval condition no dey, so e no certain
l-m-h2-b0d04-07.s.s1.r.d: B correct. For dis interval maximum value really no dey.
l-m-h2-b0d04-07.s.s1.explain: As x→0+, 1/x dey grow without end, so maximum value no dey. Di maximum-minimum theorem na for continuous functions for closed interval [a,b].
l-m-h2-b0d04-07.s.s2.model.0: Di near x reach 0, di bigger 1/x dey grow without end, so (0,1] no get maximum value. Di interval no closed, so B correct.
l-m-h2-b0d04-07.s.s2.model.1: Dem dey use di theorem wey promise maximum value only for continuity for closed interval, so for (0,1], wey open for one end, we no fit talk wetin A talk.

l-m-h2-b0d04-27.title: Di integral of x³ from −2 to 2 equal 0 or 8?
l-m-h2-b0d04-27.goal: Compare two methods or claims about di value of di definite integral of x³ from −2 to 2, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-h2-b0d04-27.material: A talk say because di interval symmetric, (di definite integral of x³ from −2 to 2)=2×(di definite integral of x³ from 0 to 2)=8. B talk say make you put −2 and 2 inside [x⁴/4], and e go give 4−4=0.
l-m-h2-b0d04-27.s.s1.o.a: A: If e symmetric, e dey always 2 times
l-m-h2-b0d04-27.s.s1.r.a: x³ negative for x<0, so e no go become 2 times.
l-m-h2-b0d04-27.s.s1.o.b: B: Di areas for both sides get opposite signs and dem cancel each other
l-m-h2-b0d04-27.s.s1.r.c: Di values 8 and 0 different, so di two no fit both correct.
l-m-h2-b0d04-27.s.s1.r.d: To put −2 and 2 inside [x⁴/4] give 4−4, so e na 0, no be 4.
l-m-h2-b0d04-27.s.s1.explain: x³ na odd function. Di x<0 part na −4 and di x>0 part na +4, so di sum na 0. Dem only dey use di 2-times rule for even functions.
l-m-h2-b0d04-27.s.s2.model.0: Because x³ negative for x<0, di integral from −2 to 0 na −4 and from 0 to 2 na 4, so di sum na 0. So B correct.
l-m-h2-b0d04-27.s.s2.model.1: Even when e symmetric, opposite signs dey cancel each other, so A, wey multiply by 2, wrong, and B, wey get 4−4=0, correct.

l-m-h2-b0d04-28.title: If you differentiate and then integrate again, you go get di original function back?
l-m-h2-b0d04-28.goal: Compare two methods or claims about di result of differentiating f(x) and then integrating again, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-h2-b0d04-28.material: To differentiate f(x)=x²+3 give 2x, and if you take indefinite integral of dis one e give x²+C. A talk say, "So if we integrate again we go get f(x)=x²+3 back exactly," and B talk say, "You need to know C separate before you go know di original function."
l-m-h2-b0d04-28.s.s1.o.a: A: 3 no get anything to do with differentiation, so e dey always 3
l-m-h2-b0d04-28.s.s1.r.a: When you differentiate, di 3 disappear, so no information dey wey fit bring am back.
l-m-h2-b0d04-28.s.s1.o.b: A: x²+3 go come back exactly
l-m-h2-b0d04-28.s.s1.r.b: Di indefinite integral na x²+C, and dem no fix C.
l-m-h2-b0d04-28.s.s1.o.c: B: E na x²+C, so you need to know C separate
l-m-h2-b0d04-28.s.s1.r.d: C no dey fixed for 0. E be 3 for begin.
l-m-h2-b0d04-28.s.s1.explain: Wen you differentiate, di constant term 3 go turn 0, so e go disappear. So di indefinite integral na x²+C, and to know di original function you need extra information say C=3.
l-m-h2-b0d04-28.s.s2.model.0: Wen you differentiate, di constant term 3 go disappear, so if you integrate again, e still go give x²+C, and na only if you know C you fit know di original function.
l-m-h2-b0d04-28.s.s2.model.1: Constant get derivative 0, so 2x no get any information about di 3, and di indefinite integral fit only be written as x²+C.

l-m-h2-b0d05-30.title: To choose 3 representatives: how the two solutions compare?
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.goal: Compare two methods or claims for the number of ways to choose 3 people wey include both boys and girls, choose the one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.material: Choose 3 representatives from 4 boys and 3 girls so that both boys and girls dey inside. Solution A: 7C3-4C3-3C3=30. Solution B: first choose 1 boy and 1 girl (4×3), then choose 1 from the remaining 5, so 4×3×5=60.
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.s.s1.prompt: Choose the solution wey fit pass and the reason.
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.s.s1.o.a: B right. A subtract too many cases
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.s.s1.r.a: A subtract only the cases wey get one gender from the total, so e correct.
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.s.s1.o.b: Both right. Dem just different for method, so the values different
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.s.s1.r.b: Problem get one answer, so if the two values different, one of dem wrong.
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.s.s1.o.c: A right. B count the same group of representatives many times
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.s.s1.o.d: Both wrong. You no fit solve am with combinations
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.s.s1.r.d: Na selection without order, so you fit solve am with combinations.
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.s.s1.explain: 7C3-4C3-3C3=30 correct. B count the same group 2 times, depending on who dem choose first, wey make am 60.
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.s.s2.model.0: A subtract the single-gender cases from the total, wey give 30. B count the same group twice depending on who dem choose first, so A right.
l-m-h2-b0d05-30.s.s2.model.1: Group of 2 boys and 1 girl dey repeat depending on which boy dem choose first, so B turn 60, 2 times 30.

l-m-h2-b0d05-31.title: Two ways to know whether events independent
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.goal: Compare two methods or claims for how to judge whether two events independent, choose the one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.material: When dem roll a die once, A na 'even' and B na '3 or less'. Student S: dem no look like say dem dey affect each other, so dem independent. Student T: P(A∩B)=1/6 and P(A)P(B)=1/4 different, so dem no independent.
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.s.s1.prompt: Whose judgment you fit trust pass?
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.s.s1.o.a: S: the one wey think say no influence dey
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.s.s1.r.a: Una must check independence with P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B), no be by feeling.
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.s.s1.o.b: T: the one wey check whether the product equal
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.s.s1.o.c: Both: you no fit know without to calculate
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.s.s1.r.c: You fit judge by to work out the probabilities directly.
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.s.s1.o.d: S: na one die, so dem independent
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.s.s1.r.d: Since dem use the same die face for both, dem tie together really.
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.s.s1.explain: Dem dey judge independence by P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B). Here 1/6≠1/4, so dem no independent.
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.s.s2.model.0: T compare P(A∩B)=1/6 with P(A)P(B)=1/4 by the definition and conclude say dem no independent because the values different, so T pass for trust.
l-m-h2-b0d05-31.s.s2.model.1: Feeling fit wrong, so the one wey check directly whether the product equal pass for trust. When dem use one die face for two events, dem fit tie together.

l-m-h2-b0d05-32.title: With samples of 25 and 100, how different the intervals be?
l-m-h2-b0d05-32.goal: Compare two methods or claims about the length of the confidence interval depending on the sample size, choose the one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d05-32.material: From population wey standard deviation na 10, you build confidence interval for the population mean at the same 95% confidence. Compare the interval lengths when dem sample 25 people and when dem sample 100.
l-m-h2-b0d05-32.s.s1.prompt: Which one na the correct relationship between the two interval lengths?
l-m-h2-b0d05-32.s.s1.o.b: The two lengths the same. Because the confidence level the same
l-m-h2-b0d05-32.s.s1.r.b: Even with the same confidence level, σ/√n dey change with n, so the length dey change.
l-m-h2-b0d05-32.s.s1.r.c: When n big 4 times, √n big 2 times, so the length na half.
l-m-h2-b0d05-32.s.s1.r.d: The bigger the sample, the smaller σ/√n, so the interval short pass.
l-m-h2-b0d05-32.s.s1.explain: The length dey proportional to 1/√n. √25=5 and √100=10, so with 100 people the length na half (7.84 and 3.92).
l-m-h2-b0d05-32.s.s2.model.0: The length dey proportional to σ/√n, and when n go from 25 to 100, 4 times bigger, √n become 2 times bigger, so the interval length na half.
l-m-h2-b0d05-32.s.s2.model.1: Even with the same confidence level, σ/√n na 10/5=2 and 10/10=1, so the 100-person interval half as long.

l-m-h2-b0d05-33.title: Why the two ways to find 8P3 give the same value?
l-m-h2-b0d05-33.goal: Compare two methods or claims for the two ways to find 8P3, choose the one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d05-33.material: Two students calculate how many ways 3 out of 8 people fit receive gold, silver, and bronze medals in order. Student A: 8×7×6=336. Student B: first choose 3 people (8C3=56), then decide di medal order, 56×6=336. Think about why di values dey equal.
l-m-h2-b0d05-33.s.s1.prompt: Which one na di correct reason why di two values equal?
l-m-h2-b0d05-33.s.s1.o.a: To multiply by di order 3! of di 3 wey dem choose make dem equal
l-m-h2-b0d05-33.s.s1.r.c: Dat one na wrong direction. 8P3 na 8C3 multiplied by 6.
l-m-h2-b0d05-33.s.s1.o.d: Di two values just equal by chance
l-m-h2-b0d05-33.s.s1.r.d: 8P3=8C3×3!, so e no be coincidence, e dey always true.
l-m-h2-b0d05-33.s.s1.explain: If you multiply 8C3, wey choose 3 people, by 3!=6, di orders of those 3, e give 8P3. 56×6=336 and nPr=nCr×r!.
l-m-h2-b0d05-33.s.s2.model.0: To choose 3 people with 8C3 and multiply by 3!=6, di ways to line di 3 up, count di order too, so e equal 8P3.
l-m-h2-b0d05-33.s.s2.model.1: Permutation na combination multiplied by r!, di number of orders, so 56×6=336 equal 8×7×6.

l-m-h2-b0d05-34.title: When e dey fine to approximate with normal distribution?
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.goal: Compare two methods or claims about when binomial distribution fit dey approximated by normal distribution, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.material: Di number of heads X for coin tosses follow binomial distribution. A: approximate X by N(200, 100) for 400 tosses. B: approximate X by N(5, 2.5) for 10 tosses. Decide which normal approximation you fit trust pass.
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.s.s1.prompt: Which one you fit trust pass, and why?
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.s.s1.o.a: B: di mean small, so e more accurate
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.s.s1.r.a: With few tosses, di bars of di binomial distribution rough, so di approximation no too accurate.
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.s.s1.o.b: Both get p=0.5, so dem equally accurate
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.s.s1.r.b: Even if p dey di same, di bigger n be, di better di approximation.
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.s.s1.o.c: A: n big, so e near normal distribution
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.s.s1.o.d: B: di variance small, so e more accurate
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.s.s1.r.d: Small variance alone no dey make di approximation better.
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.s.s1.explain: Di bigger n be, di more di shape of di binomial distribution dey near di bell-shaped normal distribution. With 10 tosses few bars dey, so dem fit easily no match.
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.s.s2.model.0: Binomial distribution dey near normal distribution as n dey grow, so A, wey get 400 tosses, get more accurate approximation wey you fit trust.
l-m-h2-b0d05-34.s.s2.model.1: B get only 11 possible values, so e differ well well from smooth curve, and A with n=400 you fit trust pass.

l-m-h2-b0d06-28.title: Three dice: di probability say at least one na 6
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.goal: Compare two methods or claims for how to find di probability say at least one 6 go show, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.material: Two students find di probability say at least one of three dice wey dem roll na 6. Student A: find di cases of 1, 2, and 3 dice wey show 6 separately and add dem to get 91/216. Student B: 1-(5/6)³=91/216. Di two values na di same.
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.s.s1.prompt: Which judgment correct after you compare di two methods?
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.s.s1.r.a: Di values na di same, so di accuracy na di same, and A get bigger risk to miss cases.
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.s.s1.o.b: Dem fit only use B wen di events independent
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.s.s1.r.b: Dem fit use di complement even without independence. Na only di product need independence.
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.s.s1.o.c: Di values na di same, so no difference dey between di two
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.s.s1.r.c: Even if di answers na di same, di amount of calculation and di risk of mistakes different.
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.s.s1.o.d: B simple pass and e get less risk to miss cases
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.s.s1.explain: To count directly need to split am into three cases. Di complement need only one case, 'no 6 at all', so di calculation short.
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.s.s2.model.0: A must add up all di cases of 1, 2, and 3 dice wey show 6, but B find only di one case wey no get 6 at all, so e simple pass.
l-m-h2-b0d06-28.s.s2.model.1: Even though both values na di same, 91/216, A fit miss cases, so B, wey use di complement, make less mistakes.

l-m-h2-b0d06-29.s.s1.prompt: Whose judgment you fit trust pass?
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.title: If di test show positive, di person really sick?
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.goal: Compare two methods or claims for di probability of having di disease after one positive result, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.material: 1% of di population get di disease. 99% of people wey get di disease test positive, and 5% of people wey no get di disease test positive too. Student A: e accurate 99%, so positive result mean 99% chance of di disease. Student B: out of 1×10⁴ (10,000) people, 99 of di 594 positives get di disease, so about 17%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.s.s1.o.a: B: calculate di share of sick people among di positives
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.s.s1.o.b: A: di accuracy na 99%, so e na 99%
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.s.s1.r.b: 99% na di probability of positive result wen di person get di disease, so dem reverse di condition.
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.s.s1.o.c: Both: dem no fit calculate am
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.s.s1.r.c: Dem fit calculate am from di population rate and di positive rates.
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.s.s1.o.d: A: di probability of having di disease wen di result positive na 5%
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.s.s1.r.d: 5% na di probability say person wey no get di disease go test positive.
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.s.s1.explain: P(positive|disease)=0.99 and P(disease|positive) different. Of di 594 positives, 99 get di disease, so P(disease|positive)=99/594≈17%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.s.s2.model.0: B find di share 99/594 of sick people among dem wey test positive, so na calculation wey match di condition and dem fit trust am.
l-m-h2-b0d06-29.s.s2.model.1: Di probability of positive result wen person get di disease and di probability of di disease wen result positive different, so wen di disease rate low, di second one small well well.

l-m-h2-b0d06-30.title: Wen di score difference na di same, who do better?
l-m-h2-b0d06-30.goal: Compare two methods or claims for how to compare scores for different tests, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d06-30.material: Di math test get mean of 50 points and standard deviation of 5 points, and di science test get mean of 60 points and standard deviation of 10 points. Compare, in three ways, which one better relatively: di student wey get 65 for math or di student wey get 75 for science.
l-m-h2-b0d06-30.s.s1.r.a: Each test get different mean and spread, so you no fit compare raw scores.
l-m-h2-b0d06-30.s.s1.o.b: Di tests different, so dem no fit compare
l-m-h2-b0d06-30.s.s1.r.b: If you standardize, you fit compare even different tests.
l-m-h2-b0d06-30.s.s1.o.d: Di difference from di mean na di same, so di two students equal
l-m-h2-b0d06-30.s.s1.r.d: Di spreads different, so di same 15 points mean different things.
l-m-h2-b0d06-30.s.s1.explain: Standardizing give (65-50)/5=3 for math and (75-60)/10=1.5 for science. Di math student higher, e far pass from di mean.
l-m-h2-b0d06-30.s.s2.model.0: After standardizing, math 65 na Z=3 and science 75 na Z=1.5, so di math student better compare to di other.
l-m-h2-b0d06-30.s.s2.model.1: Even though di difference from di mean na di same 15 points, math dey 3σ above because im standard deviation na 5, and science dey only 1.5σ above because im standard deviation na 10, so math better.
