l-m-h2-b0d06-31.goal: Compare two methods or claims for di number of different terms for di expansion of (x+y)⁵, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d06-31.material: Two students give di number of different terms after dem expand (x+y)⁵ and combine like terms. Student A: 6. Student B: from di 5 brackets, you pick either x or y from each one, so 2⁵=32.
l-m-h2-b0d06-31.s.s1.o.a: B: 32 ways dey to choose, so 32 terms dey
l-m-h2-b0d06-31.s.s1.r.a: 32 na di number of products before dem combine. E go reduce after dem combine like terms.
l-m-h2-b0d06-31.s.s1.o.b: A: to combine di same terms give 6, from x⁵ reach y⁵
l-m-h2-b0d06-31.s.s1.o.c: Both correct. Na di difference before and after simplifying
l-m-h2-b0d06-31.s.s1.r.c: Di question ask for di number of terms after simplifying, so only A correct.
l-m-h2-b0d06-31.s.s1.r.d: With x⁵, x⁴y, ..., y⁵, 6 terms dey.
l-m-h2-b0d06-31.s.s1.explain: After simplifying, 6 dey: x⁵, x⁴y, x³y², x²y³, xy⁴, y⁵. 32 na di number of products wey dem make before dem combine.
l-m-h2-b0d06-31.s.s2.model.0: After dem combine like terms, di exponent of x take 6 values from 5 go down to 0, so 6 terms dey. 32 na di number of products before dem combine, so A correct.
l-m-h2-b0d06-31.s.s2.model.1: As many as 5 products dey wey make x⁴y, but dem combine into one term, so 6 terms dey and A judgment na di one wey fit.

l-m-h2-b0d06-32.title: Two games wey get di same expected value, dem be di same?
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.goal: Compare two methods or claims about di difference between two games wey get di same expected value, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.material: Game A: you always get 3 points. Game B: you toss coin and you get 6 points for heads and 0 points for tails. Di expected value of both games na 3 points. Choose di statement wey fit pass wey compare di two games.
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.s.s1.o.a: Di expected values dey di same, so di two games identical
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.s.s1.r.a: Even if di expected value dey di same, how di results spread out different, so dem no identical.
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.s.s1.o.b: B fit give up to 6 points, so e dey always better
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.s.s1.r.b: 0 points fit come up too, and di expected values dey di same, so you no fit talk say e dey always better.
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.s.s1.o.c: A dey always better because im score dey stay di same
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.s.s1.r.c: Which one better depend on how much you wan avoid risk.
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.s.s1.o.d: Di expected values dey di same, but di variances differ: 0 and 9
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.s.s1.explain: Di variance of A na 0, and for B e na E(X²)-9=18-9=9. Even when di means dey di same, di spread different.
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.s.s2.model.0: Di expected value of both games dey di same, 3, but di variance na 0 for A and 9 for B. So di results spread different way, and di games no be di same.
l-m-h2-b0d06-32.s.s2.model.1: Expected value alone no fit show di risk, so you need look di variance too. B split into 0 points and 6 points, so im variance na 9.

l-m-h2-b0d01-12.goal: For the base of logarithmic scale, think about all the conditions wey dey clash, choose the best compromise, then explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d01-12.material: Dem draw data wey values spread from 1 to 1,000,000 for logarithmic scale graph. Dem put one tick mark for each power of the base, and e easy to read if at least 5 and at most 8 ticks dey.

l-m-h2-b0d01-12.s.s2.model.1: Small base give too many ticks and big base give too few, so base 10, wey give suitable 7, meet both conditions.

l-m-h2-b0d01-28.goal: Think well about all di conditions wey dey fight each other for exercise plan first-day time and daily increase, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d01-28.material: You dey exercise for a minutes for di first day and you dey add d minutes every day, for 10 days. Di total for 10 days must be at least 330 minutes, and di last day must be at most 50 minutes.
l-m-h2-b0d01-28.s.s1.r.a: Di total na 290 minutes, wey no reach 330 minutes.

l-m-h2-b0d01-28.s.s1.r.d: Di total na 300 minutes, wey no reach 330 minutes.

l-m-h2-b0d02-09.title: To Reduce Noise: Meeting Decibels and Cost Together
l-m-h2-b0d02-09.goal: For soundproofing work to reduce noise, weigh all the conditions wey dey clash, choose the best compromise, then explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d02-09.material: The noise level na L=10log(I/I₀) dB. We wan reduce the current 80 dB noise to 60 dB or below. Dem set the soundproofing work by which fraction (1 out of how many) the sound intensity I reduce to, and the cost must be at most 50.
l-m-h2-b0d02-09.s.s1.r.a: 80−10=70 dB, wey no reach 60 dB or below.
l-m-h2-b0d02-09.s.s1.r.b: 80−10log50≈63 dB, wey no reach 60 dB or below.
l-m-h2-b0d02-09.s.s1.r.d: E reduce the noise to 50 dB, but the cost of 90 pass the limit of 50.
l-m-h2-b0d02-09.s.s1.explain: If you reduce the intensity to 1/100, e lower the level by 10log100=20 dB to 60 dB, and the cost of 40 dey inside the limit.
l-m-h2-b0d02-09.s.s2.model.0: If you reduce the intensity to 1/100, e lower the level by 20 dB to 60 dB, and the cost of 40 na at most 50, so both conditions meet.
l-m-h2-b0d02-09.s.s2.model.1: 1/10 and 1/50 no go work because the noise still dey above 60 dB, and 1/1000 no go work because the cost pass 50, so na 1/100 remain.

l-m-h2-b0d02-20.title: Work for When Ships Dey Pass for High Tide: When E Suppose Start?
l-m-h2-b0d02-20.goal: For di start time of work wey meet di water-depth condition, think about all di conditions wey dey fight each other, pick di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d02-20.material: Di water depth of a harbor na h(t)=4+2sin(πt/6) m (t na di time, 0≤t≤12). A ship fit pass only when di depth at least 5 m, and di passing work dey last 2 hours.
l-m-h2-b0d02-20.s.s1.prompt: Which one na good start time for di work?
l-m-h2-b0d02-20.s.s1.r.a: For t=0.5 di depth na like 4.5 m, so e don dey below 5 m from di start.
l-m-h2-b0d02-20.s.s1.r.c: Di work dey last reach t=5.5, but di depth by dat time na like 4.5 m, wey dey below 5 m.
l-m-h2-b0d02-20.s.s1.r.d: Di work dey last reach t=6.5, and for t=6 di depth na 4 m, wey dey below 5 m.
l-m-h2-b0d02-20.s.s1.explain: Di depth at least 5 m when 1≤t≤5. A 2-hour job must start inside 1≤t≤3.
l-m-h2-b0d02-20.s.s2.model.0: h(t)≥5 dey true when 1≤t≤5, so make 2-hour job fit enter dis range, e must start for t=2.
l-m-h2-b0d02-20.s.s2.model.1: Di time wey di depth at least 5 m run from t=1 reach t=5, wey be 4 hours, so if dem work from t=2 reach 4, di depth go dey above 5 m all di time.

l-m-h2-b0d02-24.material: For one triangular flower bed, two sides na 6 m and 8 m, and we go choose di included angle θ between dem. Di area must be at least 20 ㎡, and di third side (di fence) must be at most 12 m.

l-m-h2-b0d02-24.s.s2.model.0: With θ=90°, di area na 24 ㎡, wey at least 20, and di third side na 10 m, wey at most 12, so both conditions dey met.
l-m-h2-b0d02-24.s.s2.model.1: If θ small di area no go reach, and if θ big di third side go long pass, so di only candidate wey satisfy both na 90°.

l-m-h2-b0d02-31.material: Dem stack cards with 1 card for di first row, 3 for di second, 5 for di third, and so on, dey increase by 2 each row. Dem fit use only up to 50 cards, and we wan at least 6 rows, dey stack as many rows as possible.

l-m-h2-b0d02-31.s.s2.model.0: n rows dey use 1+3+…+(2n−1)=n² cards, so 7 rows na 49 cards, wey at most 50 and di most among 6 rows or more.
l-m-h2-b0d02-31.s.s2.model.1: 8 rows need 64 cards and e pass di limit, so e no go work, and 6 rows na 36 cards, wey be fewer than 7 rows, so 7 rows na di best one.

l-m-h2-b0d03-18.material: Use the wall as one side and use all 60m of fencing for the other three sides to make rectangular field. The side wey parallel to the wall must be at most 24m, and the bigger the area, the better. The width x na the side wey perpendicular to the wall.

l-m-h2-b0d03-21.title: If we raise the price, profit go increase? The sales condition
l-m-h2-b0d03-21.goal: Weigh all the conditions wey dey clash for the selling price of one item, choose the best compromise, then explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d03-21.material: One item cost 20 won each, and when di price na p won, di number wey dem sell na (100−p). Di profit na (p−20)(100−p), and because of stock, dem must sell at least 50. Choose di integer price wey get di greatest profit.
l-m-h2-b0d03-21.s.s1.prompt: Which price give di greatest profit while e dey follow di conditions?
l-m-h2-b0d03-21.s.s1.r.a: E follow di conditions, but di profit na 1200, wey small pass.
l-m-h2-b0d03-21.s.s1.r.b: E follow di conditions, but di profit na 1375, wey small pass 1500 for p=50.
l-m-h2-b0d03-21.s.s1.r.d: Di profit na di greatest, but dem sell only 40, wey small pass 50.
l-m-h2-b0d03-21.s.s1.explain: Di profit big pass for p=60, but 100−p≥50 mean p≤50. Inside dat range, di profit big pass for p=50, wey be 1500.
l-m-h2-b0d03-21.s.s2.model.0: Dem no allow p=60 because dem sell only 40. For p≤50, di profit dey get bigger as p dey get bigger, so p=50 na di best.
l-m-h2-b0d03-21.s.s2.model.1: Because of di sales condition, p≤50, and di profit (p−20)(100−p) dey increase reach 60, so e big pass for p=50, wey be 1500.

l-m-h2-b0d03-30.title: Flower bed area condition and how to save material: which width?
l-m-h2-b0d03-30.goal: Weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other for di width of a flower bed, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d03-30.material: Di flower bed na di part wey −a≤x≤a between di graph of y=4−x² and di x-axis (unit: m). Di area must be at least 9m², and di width 2a suppose short as e fit so dat dem go save material.
l-m-h2-b0d03-30.s.s1.prompt: Which a give di shortest width wey follow di conditions?
l-m-h2-b0d03-30.s.s1.r.a: Di area na about 7.33, wey small pass 9.
l-m-h2-b0d03-30.s.s1.r.b: Di area na about 8.45, wey small pass 9.
l-m-h2-b0d03-30.s.s1.r.d: E follow di conditions, but di width wide pass, so e use more material.
l-m-h2-b0d03-30.s.s1.explain: Di area na 8a−2a³/3. When a=1.4, e na about 9.37, wey at least 9, and 1.2 give about 8.45, wey no reach. Among di choices, 1.4 na di shortest.
l-m-h2-b0d03-30.s.s2.model.0: For a=1.4 di area 8a−2a³/3≈9.37 na at least 9, and 1.2 give 8.45, wey no reach, so among di choices di shortest width na a=1.4.
l-m-h2-b0d03-30.s.s2.model.1: a=1.5 also follow di condition with area 9.75, but im width wide pass, so a=1.4 better for saving material.

l-m-h2-b0d04-18.title: Box wey get fixed frame length: wetin go happen if height get limit?
l-m-h2-b0d04-18.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey fight each other for di side length of box wey get square base, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d04-18.material: Dem make rectangular frame from 120 cm of wire. Di base na square wey get side x, and di height na h. If dem use all di wire, 2x+h=30. Bigger volume x²h better, and di height must be 8 cm or less.
l-m-h2-b0d04-18.s.s1.prompt: Which x go give di biggest volume as e still dey keep di height condition?
l-m-h2-b0d04-18.s.s1.r.b: Di volume na di biggest, 1000, but di height na 10, wey pass 8.
l-m-h2-b0d04-18.s.s1.r.d: E meet di conditions, but di volume 864 small pass 968 wey x=11 give.
l-m-h2-b0d04-18.s.s1.explain: V=x²(30−2x) biggest for x=10, but di height 30−2x≤8 mean say x≥11. For x≥10, V dey reduce, so x=11 na di best.
l-m-h2-b0d04-18.s.s2.model.0: x=10 give di biggest volume, but di height 10 pass 8, so dem no allow am. Because di volume dey reduce for x≥10, di smallest x wey meet di condition, x=11, na di best.
l-m-h2-b0d04-18.s.s2.model.1: Di height 30−2x≤8 give x≥11, and for dis range di volume dey small as x dey big, so di volume biggest for x=11, wey be 968.

l-m-h2-b0d04-29.title: Fill di water tank reach at least 20 L without say e overflow
l-m-h2-b0d04-29.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey fight each other for di time to fill di water tank, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d04-29.material: Water dey enter at rate of v(t)=2t (L/min). Dem must fill di tank reach at least 20 L, and e capacity na 25 L, so e no must overflow. Di time T minutes wey dem go close di water suppose be as early as possible.
l-m-h2-b0d04-29.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di earliest time T wey meet all di conditions?
l-m-h2-b0d04-29.s.s1.r.a: Di amount wey enter na 4²=16 L, wey no reach 20 L.
l-m-h2-b0d04-29.s.s1.r.c: E meet di conditions with 25 L, but e don pass 4.5 minutes.
l-m-h2-b0d04-29.s.s1.r.d: E turn 36 L and e overflow di 25 L capacity.
l-m-h2-b0d04-29.s.s1.explain: Di amount wey enter na T² L. T=4 give 16 L, wey too small, and 4.5 give 20.25 L, wey meet di conditions. E finish earlier pass 5 and 6.
l-m-h2-b0d04-29.s.s2.model.0: Di amount wey enter na di definite integral of 2t from 0 to T, wey be T², so e must dey between 20 and 25. For di choices, di earliest one, 4.5 minutes, give 20.25 L, so e correct.
l-m-h2-b0d04-29.s.s2.model.1: T=4 give 16 L, wey no reach, and T=6 give 36 L, wey overflow. For 4.5 and 5 wey meet di conditions, di earlier one, 4.5, na di best.

l-m-h2-b0d04-30.title: Choose stopping time wey reach at least 12 m with di least running
l-m-h2-b0d04-30.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey fight each other for di time to stop di cart at least 12 m away, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d04-30.material: Di cart velocity na v(t)=8−2t (m/s); e go stop for 4 seconds and then e go dey go back. Dem must stop am for time T seconds for place wey be at least 12 m from where e start, while di total distance wey e really travel must be di shortest.
l-m-h2-b0d04-30.s.s1.prompt: Which T go keep di conditions while e run di least?
l-m-h2-b0d04-30.s.s1.r.a: E only reach 7 m from where e start, e no reach 12 m.
l-m-h2-b0d04-30.s.s1.r.c: E meet di condition, but di distance wey e travel long pass, e be 15 m.
l-m-h2-b0d04-30.s.s1.r.d: E dey 12 m from where e start, but e turn back after 4 seconds and e travel 20 m in total.
l-m-h2-b0d04-30.s.s1.explain: Di position na 8T−T², wey be 12 m for T=2. T=6 too be 12 m, but 4 m of turning back after 4 seconds join am, so di distance wey e travel na 20 m.
l-m-h2-b0d04-30.s.s2.model.0: For T=2 di position na 8·2−4=12 m, wey meet di condition, and as e no turn back, di distance wey e travel na 12 m, di shortest, so T=2.
l-m-h2-b0d04-30.s.s2.model.1: T=6 too get position of 12 m, but after 4 seconds e come back 4 m, so di distance wey e travel turn 20 m. Na why T=2 fit more.

l-m-h2-b0d05-35.topic: Statistical estimation (how to estimate with statistics)
l-m-h2-b0d05-35.title: Sample size between accuracy and survey cost
l-m-h2-b0d05-35.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey fight each other for di confidence interval length and di survey cost when you dey choose sample size, pick di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d05-35.material: Estimate di population mean of population wey get standard deviation 10 at 95% confidence (coefficient 1.96). Conditions: di confidence interval length na at most 2, and di survey cost 1,000 won per person with budget of at most 400,000 won.
l-m-h2-b0d05-35.s.s1.prompt: Which sample size meet both conditions?
l-m-h2-b0d05-35.s.s1.r.a: Di length na around 3.92, wey long pass 2. Di accuracy condition no meet.
l-m-h2-b0d05-35.s.s1.r.b: Di length na around 2.48, wey long pass 2. Di accuracy condition still no meet.
l-m-h2-b0d05-35.s.s1.r.d: Di length short, but di cost na 900,000 won, wey pass di budget.
l-m-h2-b0d05-35.s.s1.explain: Di length na 2×1.96×10/√n=39.2/√n. For n=385 e na around 1.998, at most 2, and di cost na 385,000 won, wey dey inside di budget.
l-m-h2-b0d05-35.s.s2.model.0: Di length na 39.2/√n, so n must be at least 385 make e be at most 2, and 385 people cost 385,000 won, wey dey inside di budget, so e fit.
l-m-h2-b0d05-35.s.s2.model.1: 100 and 250 people give lengths wey long pass 2, and 900 people pass di budget, so only 385 people meet both conditions.

l-m-h2-b0d05-36.title: Game wey dem choose between di entry fee and di risk of getting nothing
l-m-h2-b0d05-36.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey fight each other for di entry fee and di risk of getting nothing for di game, pick di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d05-36.material: Choose game wey get entry fee of 1,000 won. Conditions: di expected amount wey you go receive na at least di entry fee, and di probability say you go receive nothing na at most 70%. Game A: 1,500 won with probability 1/2. Game B: 12,000 won with probability 1/10. Game C: 100,000 won with probability 1/100. Game D: 3,000 won with probability 2/5.
l-m-h2-b0d05-36.s.s1.r.a: Di expected value na 750 won, wey small pass di entry fee of 1,000 won.
l-m-h2-b0d05-36.s.s1.r.b: Di expected value na 1,200 won, but di probability of getting nothing na 90%.
l-m-h2-b0d05-36.s.s1.r.c: Di expected value na 1,000 won, but di probability of getting nothing na 99%.
l-m-h2-b0d05-36.s.s1.explain: D get expected value 3,000×2/5=1,200 won, at least 1,000 won, and di probability of getting nothing na 3/5=60%, at most 70%.
l-m-h2-b0d05-36.s.s2.model.0: D get expected value 1,200 won, at least di entry fee, and di probability of getting nothing na 60%, at most 70%, so e meet both conditions.
l-m-h2-b0d05-36.s.s2.model.1: B and C get enough expected value but high probability of getting nothing, and A expected value no reach, so only D meet both conditions.

l-m-h2-b0d05-37.material: You dey create password. Use only one kind of character: di digits 0~9 or di 26 lowercase English letters, and you no fit use di same character two times. Conditions: length at most 5, and at least 100,000 possible cases. Shorter one easy to remember.

l-m-h2-b0d05-37.s.s1.explain: 4 lowercase letters give 26×25×24×23=358,800 ways, and di length na at most 5 too. 3 letters no reach and 6 letters too long.
l-m-h2-b0d05-37.s.s2.model.0: 4 lowercase letters give 358,800 ways, at least 100,000, and di length na at most 5, so na di shortest option wey meet all three conditions.
l-m-h2-b0d05-37.s.s2.model.1: 5 digits and 3 lowercase letters get too few cases and 6 pass 5 characters, so 4 lowercase letters fit.

l-m-h2-b0d05-38.title: How many questions suppose be di passing standard?
l-m-h2-b0d05-38.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey fight each other for how to stop people wey dey guess from passing while you let skilled students pass, pick di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d05-38.material: For 20-question test, you pass if k or more correct. Student wey dey guess (correct rate 0.2) suppose pass at most 1% of di time, and skilled student (correct rate 0.8) at least 95%. Pass rates (guessing/skilled): k=6 around 20%/100%, k=8 around 3%/100%, k=10 around 0.3%/99.9%, k=14 around 0%/91%.
l-m-h2-b0d05-38.s.s1.prompt: Which standard k meet both conditions?
l-m-h2-b0d05-38.s.s1.r.a: Di pass rate of di student wey dey guess na around 20%, far pass 1%.
l-m-h2-b0d05-38.s.s1.r.b: Di pass rate of di student wey dey guess na around 3%, pass 1%.
l-m-h2-b0d05-38.s.s1.r.d: Di guessing pass rate low, but di pass rate of di skilled student na 91%, wey no reach 95%.
l-m-h2-b0d05-38.s.s1.explain: With k=10, guessing na around 0.3%, at most 1%, and di skilled na 99.9%, at least 95%. For 6 and 8 guessing high, and for 14 di skilled low.
l-m-h2-b0d05-38.s.s2.model.0: With k=10, di pass rate of di student wey dey guess na around 0.3%, at most 1%, and di skilled student own na 99.9%, at least 95%, so both conditions meet.
l-m-h2-b0d05-38.s.s2.model.1: Low standard dey let people wey dey guess pass and high one dey fail skilled students, so k=10, wey balance di two conditions, fit.

l-m-h2-b0d06-33.title: How to prepare di fewest kinds of items for set menus
l-m-h2-b0d06-33.goal: For setup wey meet di conditions on di number of choices and di number of kinds to prepare, weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d06-33.material: One set get 1 main dish and 1 drink. Conditions: customers fit choose from at least 12 sets, and di total number of menu kinds to prepare (number of main dishes + number of drinks) suppose small as e fit be.
l-m-h2-b0d06-33.s.s1.prompt: Which setup meet di conditions best?
l-m-h2-b0d06-33.s.s1.r.b: Dat one make 3×3=9 sets, wey no reach 12.
l-m-h2-b0d06-33.s.s1.r.c: 12 sets dey, but di total number of kinds na 8, wey more.
l-m-h2-b0d06-33.s.s1.r.d: 15 sets dey, but di total number of kinds na 8, wey more.
l-m-h2-b0d06-33.s.s1.explain: By di multiplication rule, 3×4=12 sets, and di total number of kinds na 7. Di other setups give less than 12 sets or get bigger total of 8.
l-m-h2-b0d06-33.s.s2.model.0: 3 main dishes and 4 drinks make 3×4=12 sets, wey meet di condition, and di total of 7 kinds na di smallest, so e fit best.
l-m-h2-b0d06-33.s.s2.model.1: 3×3=9 no reach, and 2×6 and 5×3 give at least 12 sets but get total of 8 kinds, so di setup wey get 3 and 4 kinds, wey total 7, fit best.

l-m-h2-b0d06-34.title: How wide di part specification suppose be?
l-m-h2-b0d06-34.goal: For allowed range wey meet di conditions on defect rate and spec width, weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d06-34.material: Part length follow normal distribution wey get mean of 100 mm and standard deviation of 2 mm. Part wey dey outside di spec (100±k mm) na defective. Conditions: defect rate of 10% or less, and di spec suppose narrow as e fit be. Inside mean±1σ na around 68%, and inside ±2σ na around 95%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-34.s.s1.prompt: Which spec meet di conditions best?
l-m-h2-b0d06-34.s.s1.r.a: Dis na ±0.5σ range, wey narrow pass ±1σ (around 68%), so more than 32% go be defective.
l-m-h2-b0d06-34.s.s1.r.b: With ±1σ range, only around 68% dey pass, so around 32% dey defective.
l-m-h2-b0d06-34.s.s1.r.d: Almost nothing defective, but e wide pass wetin e need to be.
l-m-h2-b0d06-34.s.s1.explain: ±4 mm na ±2σ, so around 95% dey pass and around 5% dey defective, wey be 10% or less. ±8 mm wide pass, and ±2 mm or less get plenty defects.
l-m-h2-b0d06-34.s.s2.model.0: ±4 mm na di mean±2σ, so around 95% dey pass and around 5% dey defective, wey be 10% or less, and e narrow pass ±8 mm.
l-m-h2-b0d06-34.s.s2.model.1: ±1 and ±2 mm na ±1σ or less, so 68% or less dey pass and too many defects dey, and ±8 mm wide for no reason, so ±4 mm fit best.

l-m-h2-b0d06-35.topic: Statistical estimation (how to estimate with statistics)
l-m-h2-b0d06-35.title: How to choose between confidence level and interval length
l-m-h2-b0d06-35.goal: For estimation method wey meet di conditions on confidence level and confidence interval length, weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d06-35.material: Dem sample 100 people from population wey get population standard deviation of 10. Conditions: confidence level of 95% or more, and confidence interval length of 4 or less. Di length na 2z×σ/√n, and z na 1.645 for 90% confidence, 1.96 for 95%, 2.33 for 98%, and 2.58 for 99%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-35.s.s1.r.a: Di length short at 3.29, but di confidence level no reach 95%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-35.s.s1.r.c: Di confidence level high, but di length na 4.66, wey pass 4.
l-m-h2-b0d06-35.s.s1.r.d: Di confidence level high, but di length na 5.16, wey pass 4.
l-m-h2-b0d06-35.s.s1.explain: Di length na 2z×10/10=2z. For 95% e na 3.92, wey be 4 or less; 98% and 99% pass 4, and 90% no get enough confidence.
l-m-h2-b0d06-35.s.s2.model.0: For 95%, di length na 2×1.96=3.92, wey be 4 or less, and di confidence level na 95% or more too, so both conditions meet.
l-m-h2-b0d06-35.s.s2.model.1: 90% no get enough confidence, and 98% and 99% get lengths wey pass 4, so only 95% fit between di two conditions.

l-m-h2-b0d06-36.title: Di smallest question bank wey get enough test versions
l-m-h2-b0d06-36.goal: For question bank wey meet di conditions on di number of test versions and di number of questions, weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d06-36.material: You dey make test by choosing 5 questions from di question bank. Di order no matter. Conditions: at least 100 different tests, and di number of questions for di bank suppose small as e fit be.
l-m-h2-b0d06-36.s.s1.prompt: Which number of questions meet di conditions best?
l-m-h2-b0d06-36.s.s1.r.c: 10C5=252 tests, but 9 questions don already do, so dis one get more questions.
l-m-h2-b0d06-36.s.s1.r.d: 12C5=792 tests, but dat one pass wetin we need.
l-m-h2-b0d06-36.s.s1.explain: 9C5=126 tests na at least 100, and 8C5=56 no reach. Di fewest questions na 9.
l-m-h2-b0d06-36.s.s2.model.0: 9 questions give 9C5=126 tests, wey be at least 100, while 8 questions give only 56, so 9 na di fewest questions wey meet di condition.
l-m-h2-b0d06-36.s.s2.model.1: 10 and 12 questions meet di condition too but get more questions, so 9 questions fit best.

l-m-h2-b0d06-37.topic: Probability of independent trials (trials wey no depend on each other)
l-m-h2-b0d06-37.title: How to balance failure probability and number installed
l-m-h2-b0d06-37.goal: For number of alarms wey meet di conditions on failure probability and number installed, weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h2-b0d06-37.material: One alarm dey fail with probability 0.2, and di failures independent of each other. If dem install several, no alarm go dey only when all of dem fail. Conditions: probability of no alarm of 1% or less, and di number installed suppose small as e fit be.
l-m-h2-b0d06-37.s.s1.prompt: Which number installed meet di conditions best?
l-m-h2-b0d06-37.s.s1.r.a: Di probability of no alarm na 0.2, far above 1%.
l-m-h2-b0d06-37.s.s1.r.d: E na 0.0016, so di condition meet, but 3 alarms don already do, so dis one more.
l-m-h2-b0d06-37.s.s1.explain: With 3 alarms, 0.2³=0.008, wey be 1% or less, and with 2 alarms e na 4%. Di smallest number wey meet di condition na 3.
l-m-h2-b0d06-37.s.s2.model.0: With 3 alarms, di probability say all of dem fail na 0.2³=0.008, wey be 1% or less, and with 2 alarms e na 4%, so 3 na di smallest number wey meet di condition.
l-m-h2-b0d06-37.s.s2.model.1: 4 alarms meet di condition too, but 3 do, so 3 fit best to keep di number installed small.
